Or it may be a figure of speech, as if it were said to the covenant: "Why were you broken?" It is personified as if it were a being that is asked why it was broken, indicating its obedience to the breaking and the consequences that follow from breaking it, just as in His words: ﴿And when the buried girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾ [al-Takwir: 8], according to the reading with the *lam* silent and the *ta* of address with a kasra. It has also been said that there is an omitted modifier, meaning: indeed the one who made the covenant will be questioned about it if he does not fulfill it.

Then He commanded the fulfillment of measure and the use of the straight balance, which pertains to dealings in wealth. In His words ﴿And fulfill the measure﴾ there is an indication that the measuring is the seller's duty, because that is not said to the buyer. Al-Hasan said: "*Al-qistas* is the steelyard, which is the *filastun*, also called *qarastun*." Mujahid said: "*Al-qistas* is justice, not an instrument." The two brothers and Hafs read it with a kasra on the *qaf*; the rest of the seven read it with a damma. Both are dialectal forms. A group read with substitution of the first *sin* by a *sad*. Ibn Atiyyah said: "The word is for emphasis, derived from *qist* (justice)." End quote. It is not possible that it derives from *qist*, because the roots differ: *qist* has the root q-s-t, while this has q-s-t-s, unless one posits that the *sin* at the end is an added letter, like the *sin* in *qudmus*, *dughbus*, and *urfas*. That is possible, but it is not one of the recognized positions for the addition of *sin*. The restriction with His words ﴿when you measure﴾ means: at the time of your measuring, as an emphasis, and so that the fulfillment is not delayed by giving less and then making up the difference later. Thus the fulfillment does not lag behind the time of measuring.

﴿That is better﴾, that is, the fulfillment and the weighing, because in it hearts are made content through being characterized by justice and by delivering what is right. ﴿And better in outcome﴾, that is, in its end, since no burden of responsibility remains on the one who fulfills and weighs, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. *Ta'wil* comes from *ma'al*, which means the return, as in His words: "better in return, better in reward, better in hope." Its outcome is better because he is known for guarding against fraud, so people rely on him in transactions, and hearts are inclined toward him.

﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge; indeed the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned﴾. ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, nor will you reach the mountains in height. All that — its evil is ever hateful in the sight of your Lord. That is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. And do not make with God another deity, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished.﴾

When He commanded three things — the fulfillment of the covenant, the fulfillment of measure, and weighing with the straight balance — He followed them with three prohibitions: "and do not pursue," "and do not walk," and "and do not make." The meaning of "*wa la taqfu*" (and do not pursue) is: do not follow what you have no knowledge of, whether in speech or action. He forbade us to say what we do not know and to act upon what we do not know. This includes the prohibition of blind following (taqlid), because it is following without knowing its soundness. Ibn Abbas said: "Its meaning: do not accuse anyone of what you do not know." Qatadah said: "Do not say: 'I saw' when you did not see, 'I heard' when you did not hear, and 'I knew' when you did not know." Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "Do not bear false witness." Ibn Atiyyah said: "This word is used for slander and defamation." End quote. In a hadith: "Whoever accuses a believer of what is not in him, God will confine him in the mire of ruin (radghat al-khabal) until he produces the way out." In another hadith: "We are the sons of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah; you do not accuse us, nor do we disown our father." From this is the saying of al-Nabighah al-Ja'di:

*Like statues, noble of nose, sitting still, the rain-clouds' sweetness among them, they do not follow the accusations.*

And al-Kumayt said:

*I do not strike the innocent without a crime, nor do I accuse the nurses if they are accused.*

Here is the translation of the passage.

The gist of this is that He forbade following what one has no knowledge of, and this is a universal principle under which many categories fall. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Those who oppose ijtihad have used this as evidence, but it is not valid, because that (conjecture) is a kind of knowledge, and the Sharia has established predominant opinion (ghalib al-zann) in the place of knowledge and commanded acting upon it." End of quotation.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿ولا تَقْفُ﴾ with the waw elided, as a jussive of qafa (تَقْفُ, from qafa, "to follow"). Zayd ibn 'Ali read "ولا تَقْفُو" with the waw retained, as the poet said:

"You satirized Zabban, then came apologizing / for the satire of Zabban; you did not satirize and you did not leave off."

Retaining the waw, the ya', and the alif with the jussive is a dialectal usage among some Arabs and a poetic necessity for others.

Mu'adh al-Qari read ﴿ولا تَقْفُ﴾ on the pattern of تَقُلْ, from qaafa yaqoofu. The Arabs say: "quftu atharahu" and "qafawtu atharahu" (I followed his track), and both are two dialects, given the existence of their derivational forms, like jabadha and jadhaba. Qa'a al-jamalu al-naqata and qa'aha (the camel mounted the she-camel) when he mounted her. Qaf is not a metathesis of qafa, as the author of al-Lawami' allowed.

Al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿والفُؤادَ﴾ with a fatha on the fa' and waw: the hamza was changed to waw after the damma in al-fu'ad, and then the heart was retained with the fatha. It is a dialect of ﴿الفُؤادُ﴾ [al-Najm: 11]. Abu Hatim and others rejected it. Moreover, it does not attach to a verb ('alam), because its complement would precede it.

Al-Hawfi said: it is attached to what (li-ka) is attached to, namely the stable predicate (al-istiqrar), and this is not apparent. In His saying ﴿إنَّ السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ there is evidence that knowledge is derived from the senses and from the intellects. This came in the Qur'anic order: beginning with hearing, then sight, then the heart.

(Ula'ika) is a demonstrative for "those" referring to ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾, and it is a demonstrative for the masculine and feminine plural, rational and non-rational alike. Ibn 'Atiyya imagined that it is restricted to the rational, saying: "He expressed ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ with ula'ika because they are senses that perceive, and He made them accountable in this verse, so they are in the state of one who reasons, and for this reason He expressed them with ula'ika."

Sibawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, in His saying ﴿رَأيْتُهم لِي ساجِدِينَ﴾ [Yusuf: 4] said: he said "ra'aytuhum" regarding the stars, because He described them with prostration, which is an act of one who reasons, so He expressed them with the pronoun of one who reasons. Al-Zajjaj related that the Arabs express both those who reason and those who do not with ula'ika, and he and al-Tabari recited:

"He blamed the dwellings after the abode of al-Liwa, / and life after those days."

As for Abu Ishaq's report about the language, it is a matter to be withheld. As for the verse, the narration in it is "al-aqwam" (the peoples). End of quotation.

What he imagined is not correct. The grammarians recite it as "ba'da ula'ika al-ayyam," and they would not recite except what was transmitted. The use of ula', ula, ula'ika and ulalika for what does not reason is not known to have any disagreement.

(Kull) is a subject, and the sentence is its predicate. The subject of (kana) returns to (kull), and likewise the pronoun in ﴿مَسْئُولًا﴾. The pronoun in (anhu) returns to "ma" in His saying ﴿ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾, so the meaning is that each of ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ will be questioned about what one has no knowledge of, that is, about the absence of what one has no knowledge of. This is the apparent meaning.

Al-Zajjaj said: they are called as witnesses, as He said: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ ألْسِنَتُهم وأيْدِيهِمْ وأرْجُلُهُمْ﴾ [al-Nur: 24]. Al-Qurtubi said in his Ahkam: the heart is questioned about what it believed, the hearing about what it heard, and the sight about what it saw.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: Allah the Exalted questions a person's hearing, sight and heart about what he said that he had no knowledge of, so his denial comes from his own limbs, and that is the utmost disgrace.

It was said: the pronoun in (kana) and ﴿مَسْئُولًا﴾ refer to the one who follows what he has no knowledge of, and the pronoun in (anhu) refers to (kull). Thus this is an iltifat (shift), since if it were in the second person, the construction would be "kullu ula'ika kunta 'anhu mas'ula."

Al-Zamakhshari said: "anhu" is in the place of the nominative as the agent, meaning each one of them was questioned about it, so "mas'ul" is attributed to the prepositional phrase, like "al-maghdub" in His saying ﴿غَيْرِ المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Fatiha: 7]. It is said to a person: why did you hear what it was not permissible for you to hear? Why did you look at what it was not permissible for you to look at? Why did you resolve upon what it was not permissible for you to resolve upon? End of quotation.

What he went to, that "anhu" is in the place of the nominative as agent, and by this he means that it is a non-named object, is not permissible. This is because the prepositional phrase and what takes the place of the agent, whether a direct object, a verbal noun or an adverbial, under their conditions, function as the agent. Just as the agent may not be fronted, so too what functions like it and takes its place. So when you say "ghadiba 'ala Zayd," it is not permissible to say "'ala Zayd ghadiba," unlike "ghadibtu 'ala Zayd," where "'ala Zayd ghadibtu" is permissible. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas has related the consensus of the grammarians that a prepositional phrase that takes the place of the agent may not be fronted before the verb. He mentioned this in his book al-Muqni'. So ﴿عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا﴾ is not like ﴿المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, because in ﴿عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا﴾ the prepositional phrase is fronted, while in ﴿المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ it is delayed. Al-Zamakhshari's statement "wa lima nazarta ma lam yahill laka" omitted "ila," and this is not permissible except in poetic necessity, since "nazara" is transitive with "ila," so the construction should have been "wa lima nazarta ila ma lam yahill laka," as he said "al-nazar ilayhi," thus transitive with "ila."

(Maraḥan) is accusative as a circumstantial state, meaning "marihan" (exulting), as you say "ja'a Zayd rakdan," meaning "rakidan" (running). Or it is accusative by eliding a modifier, meaning "dha maraḥ" (possessed of exultation). Some allowed that it be an object of purpose: "wa la tamshi fi al-ard limaraḥ" (do not walk on the earth for exultation). This does not appear. It has preceded that maraḥ is joy and exhilaration in ease and happiness, and it seems it was implicitly given the meaning of arrogance (al-ikhtiyal), because the predominance of joy and happiness is accompanied by haughtiness and arrogance. For this reason it is given as the cause by His saying ﴿إنَّكَ لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الأرْضَ﴾.

A group, as transmitted by Ya'qub, read "maraḥan" with a kasra on the ra', and it is a state: do not walk arrogant and haughty. Mujahid said: "You will not tear the earth with your walking on your heels in pride and luxury, and you will not reach the mountains" with walking on the fronts of your feet in boasting. (Tulan) — the interpretation is that your power does not reach this extent, so that would be a means to arrogance. Al-Zajjaj said: "Do not walk on the earth" arrogant, boastful, and its counterpart is ﴿وعِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلى الأرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾ [al-Furqan: 63] and ﴿اقْصِدْ في مَشْيِكَ﴾ [Luqman: 19], and ﴿ولا تَمْشِ في الأرْضِ مَرَحًا إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ﴾ [Luqman: 18].

Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الأرْضَ﴾ means you will not make a rent in it by your treading on it and the severity of your stamping, ﴿ولَنْ تَبْلُغَ الجِبالَ طُولًا﴾ by your stretching yourself, and this is a mockery of the arrogant.

Al-Jarrah al-A'rabi read "﴿لَنْ تَخْرِقَ﴾" with a damma on the ra'. Abu Hatim said: this dialect is not known. It was said: by this is indicated that man is confined between two inanimate things, weak in affecting them by tearing or reaching height, and whoever is in this position is not fit for arrogance.

The poet said:

"Do not walk above the earth except in humility, / for beneath it are people who are higher than you."

The better parsing of His saying ﴿طُولًا﴾ is as a specification (tamyiz), meaning your height will not reach the mountains. Al-Hawfi said: ﴿طُولًا﴾ is accusative as a circumstantial state, and the agent of the state is (tabluga), and it may be that the agent is (takhraqa), and ﴿طُولًا﴾ means "mutatawil" (stretching). End of quotation.

Abu al-Baqa said: ﴿طُولًا﴾ is a verbal noun in the place of a state from the subject or the object, and it may be a specification, an object of purpose, and a verbal noun from the meaning of (tabluga). End of quotation.

The two Haramis (Ibn Kathir and Nafi' — Meccan and Medinan), Abu 'Amr, Abu Ja'far and al-A'raj read "sayyi'atan" in the accusative and feminine. The rest of the Seven, and al-Hasan and Masruq, read ﴿سَيِّئُهُ﴾ with a damma on the hamza, as a construct with the masculine third-person pronoun. 'Abd Allah read "sayyi'atuhu" in the plural as a construct with the pronoun, and also from him "sayyi'at" without it, and also from him "kana khabithuhu."

As for the first reading, the apparent meaning is that this refers to the verbal nouns of the two prohibitions preceding, namely following what one has no knowledge of, and walking on the earth exultantly. It was said: it refers to all the prohibitions mentioned earlier in this sura. "Sayyi'atan" is the predicate of kana and is feminine; then He said "makruhan," which is masculine. Al-Zamakhshari said: sayyi'a in the category of nouns is like dhanb (sin), and the noun has lost the rule of adjectives, so no account is taken of its feminine form, and there is no difference between one who reads "sayyi'atan" and one who reads "sayyi'an." Do you not see that you say "al-zina sayyi'a" just as you say "al-sariqa sayyi'a," so you do not distinguish in attributing it to masculine or feminine. End of quotation. And this is a good explanation.

It was said: "makruhan" was mentioned according to the wording of (kull). They permitted that "makruhan" be a second predicate of kana according to the view of one who permits multiple predicates of kana, and that it be an apposition to sayyi'a, though apposition with a derived noun is weak, and that it be a state from the pronoun concealed in the adverbial preceding it, the adverbial being in the place of a qualifier. It was said: it is also permissible that it be an attribute of sayyi'a: since its feminine is metaphorical, it may be described by a masculine. This was deemed weak, because the permissibility of this is only when the verb with a metaphorical feminine subject precedes; when it follows and is attributed to its pronoun, it is ugly. You say "abqala al-ardu iblalaha" (the earth sprouted its vegetation), which is eloquent, but "al-ardu abqala" is ugly.

As for one who reads "sayyi'uhu" with the masculine and the construct, then "sayyi'uhu" is the subject of kana and "makruhan" is the predicate. Since among the attributes mentioned there are both bad and good, He pointed to the whole with "dhalika," and He used the singular "sayyi'a," which is what is forbidden, so the judgment of disapproval applies to it from His saying "la taj'al" to the end of the prohibitions.

As for the reading of 'Abd Allah, it is parsed as a case in which the plural is predicated with a singular masculine, which is rare, like His saying:

"Fa inna al-hawadith awda biha"
(since misfortunes have destroyed them),

because "al-hidthan" is permissible in place of "al-hawadith." Similarly here, "kana ma yasu'u" (what displeases) stands in place of its bad deeds. That (dhalika) refers to all kinds of obligations from His saying ﴿لا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إلَهًا آخَرَ﴾ [al-Isra: 22] to His saying ﴿ولا تَمْشِ في الأرْضِ مَرَحًا﴾, and they are twenty-four types of obligations, some of them commands and some prohibitions, beginning with His saying ﴿لا تَجْعَلْ﴾ [al-Isra: 22]. He concluded the verses with His saying ﴿ولا تَجْعَلْ﴾ and said "mimma awha" (of what He revealed), because that is part of what was revealed to him, since other obligations were revealed to him. ﴿مِمّا أوْحى﴾ is a predicate of that. ﴿مِنَ الحِكْمَةِ﴾ may be attached to "awha," may be an apposition to "ma," or may be a state from the accusative pronoun elided that returns to "ma." These obligations are wisdom, because their sum returns to the command of monotheism, the various acts of obedience, turning away from the world and turning toward the Hereafter; reason indicates their soundness, and they are laws in all religions that do not admit abrogation (naskh).

From Ibn 'Abbas: these verses were on the tablets of Moses, peace be upon him, the first of which is ﴿لا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إلَهًا آخَرَ﴾ [al-Isra: 22]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وكَتَبْنا لَهُ في الألْواحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-A'raf: 145]. And Allah the Exalted repeated the prohibition of association; in the first prohibition...

﴿فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَخْذُولًا﴾ [الإسراء: 22]. وفي الثاني: ﴿فَتُلْقى في جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَدْحُورًا﴾. والفرق بين «مذمومٍ» و«ملومٍ» أنّ كونه مذمومًا هو أن يُذكر أنّ الفعل الذي أقدم عليه قبيحٌ مُنكَرٌ، وكونه ملومًا هو أن يُقال له بعد الفعل والذمّ: لِمَ فعلتَ كذا؟ وما حملك عليه؟ وما استفدتَ منه إلّا إلحاقَ الضررِ بنفسك؟ فأوّلُ الأمر الذمُّ وآخرُه اللومُ. والفرق بين «مخذولٍ» و«مدحورٍ» أنّ المخذول هو المتروكُ إعانتُه ونصرُه والمفوَّضُ إلى (p-39) نفسِه، والمدحورُ المطرودُ المُبعَدُ على سبيل الإهانة له والاستخفاف به، فأوّلُ الأمر الخِذلان وآخرُه الطردُ مُهانًا. وكان وصفُ الذمّ والخِذلان يكون في الدنيا، ووصفُ اللوم والدُّحور يكون في الآخرة، ولذلك جاء ﴿فَتُلْقى في جَهَنَّمَ﴾. والخطابُ بالنهي في هذه الآيات للسامع غيرِ الرسول.

وقال الزمخشري: ولقد جعل الله ‑ عزّ وعلا ‑ فاتحتَها وخاتمتَها النهيَ عن الشرك؛ لأنّ التوحيدَ هو رأسُ كلِّ حكمةٍ وملاكُها، ومَن عَدِمه لم تنفعْه حِكَمُه وعلومُه وإن بذّ فيها الحكماءَ وحكّ بيافوخِه السماءَ، وما أغنتْ عن الفلاسفةِ أسفارُ الحِكَم وهم عن دين الله أضلُّ من النَّعَم.

﴿أفَأصْفاكم رَبُّكم بِالبَنِينَ واتَّخَذَ مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ إناثًا إنَّكم لَتَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا عَظِيمًا﴾ ﴿ولَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا في هَذا القُرْآنِ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا وما يَزِيدُهم إلّا نُفُورًا﴾ ﴿قُلْ لَوْ كانَ مَعَهُ آلِهَةٌ كَما يَقُولُونَ إذًا لابْتَغَوْا إلى ذِي العَرْشِ سَبِيلًا﴾ ﴿سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى عَمّا يَقُولُونَ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ ﴿تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّماواتُ السَّبْعُ والأرْضُ ومَن فِيهِنَّ وإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ ولَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهم إنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا﴾.

لمّا نبّه تعالى على فساد مَن أثبت لله شريكًا ونظيرًا، أتبعه بفساد طريقة مَن أثبت لله ولدًا. والاستفهامُ معناه الإنكارُ والتوبيخ، والخطابُ لِمَن اعتقد أنّ الملائكةَ بناتُ الله. ومعنى ﴿أفَأصْفاكم﴾ آثركم وخصّكم، وهذا كما قال: ﴿ألَهُ البَناتُ ولَكُمُ البَنُونَ﴾ [الطور: 39]، ﴿ألَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ ولَهُ الأُنْثى﴾ [النجم: 21]. وهذا خلافُ الحكمةِ وما عليه معقولُكم وعادتُكم، فإنّ العبيدَ لا يُؤْثَرون بأجودِ الأشياء وأصفاها من الشَّوب، ويكون أرداها وأدونها للسادات. ومعنى ﴿عَظِيمًا﴾ مُبالغًا في المنكر والقبح، حيث أضفتم إليه الأولاد، ثم حيث فضّلتم عليه تعالى أنفسَكم فجعلتم له ما تكرهون، ثم نسبةُ الملائكةِ الذين هم من شريفِ ما خلق إلى الأنوثة.

ومعنى ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ نوّعنا من جهةٍ إلى جهةٍ ومن مثالٍ إلى مثالٍ، والتصريفُ لغةً: صرفُ الشيءِ من جهةٍ إلى جهةٍ، ثم صار كنايةً عن التبيين. وقرأ الجمهور ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ بتشديد الراء. فقال: لم نجعلْه نوعًا واحدًا، بل وعدًا ووعيدًا، ومحكَمًا ومتشابهًا، وأمرًا ونهيًا، وناسخًا ومنسوخًا (نَسْخ: رفعُ حكمٍ شرعيٍّ بدليلٍ متأخرٍ)، وأخبارًا وأمثالًا، مثلَ تصريفِ الرياحِ من صَبًا ودَبورٍ وجَنوبٍ وشَمالٍ. ومفعولُ ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ على هذا المعنى محذوفٌ، وهي هذه الأشياءُ، أي: صرّفنا الأمثالَ والعِبَرَ والحِكَمَ والأحكامَ والأعلامَ. وقيل: المعنى لم نُنزِلْه مرةً واحدةً بل نجومًا، ومعناه: أكثرنا صرفَ جبريلَ إليك، والمفعولُ محذوفٌ، أي: صرّفنا جبريلَ.

وقيل: (في) زائدةٌ، أي: صرّفنا هذا القرآنَ، كما قال: ﴿وأصْلِحْ لِي في ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ [الأحقاف: 15]. وهذا ضعيفٌ؛ لأنّ «في» لا تُزاد. وقال الزمخشري: يجوز أن يريد بهذا القرآنِ إبطالَ إضافتِهم إلى الله البناتِ؛ لأنه مما صرّفه وكرّر ذكره، والمعنى: ولقد (p-40) صرّفنا القولَ في هذا المعنى، وأوقعنا التصريفَ فيه وجعلناه مكانًا للتكرير، ويجوز أن يشير بهذا (القرآنِ) إلى التنزيل، ويريد: ولقد صرّفناه، يعني هذا المعنى في مواضعَ من التنزيل، فترك الضميرَ لأنه معلومٌ. انتهى. فجعل التصريفَ خاصًّا بما دلّت عليه الآيةُ قبله، وجعل مفعولَ ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ إمّا القولَ في هذا المعنى أو المعنى، وهو الضميرُ الذي قدّره في صرّفناه، وغيرُه جعل التصريفَ عامًّا في أشياءَ فقدّر ما يشمل ما سيق له ما قبلَه وغيرَه.

وقرأ الحسنُ بتخفيف الراء. فقال صاحبُ اللوامح: هو بمعنى العامّة، يعني بالعامّة: قراءةَ الجمهور، قال: لأنّ فَعَلَ وفَعَّلَ ربما تعاقبا على معنًى واحدٍ. وقال ابن عطية: على معنى صرَفْنا فيه الناسَ إلى الهدى بالدعاء إلى الله.

وقرأ الجمهور ﴿لِيَذَّكَّرُوا﴾ أي: ليتذكّروا من التذكير، أُدغمت التاءُ في الذال. وقرأ الأخَوانِ وطلحةُ وابنُ وثّابٍ والأعمشُ «لِيَذْكُرُوا» بسكون الذال وضمّ الكاف من الذِّكْرِ أو الذُّكْرِ، أي: ليتّعظوا ويعتبروا وينظروا فيما يُحتجّ به عليهم ويطمئنّوا إليه. ﴿وما يَزِيدُهُمْ﴾ أي: التصريفُ ﴿إلّا نُفُورًا﴾ أي: بُعدًا وفرارًا عن الحق، كما قال: ﴿فَزادَتْهم رِجْسًا إلى رِجْسِهِمْ﴾ [التوبة: 125]، وقال: ﴿فَما لَهم عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ [المدثر: 49] ﴿كَأنَّهم حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾ [المدثر: 50]. والنُّفورُ من أوصاف الدوابّ الشديدةِ الشِّماس. ولمّا ذكر تعالى نسبةَ الولد إليهم وردّ عليهم في ذلك، ذكر قولَهم إنه تعالى معه آلهةٌ وردّ عليهم.

وقرأ ابنُ كثيرٍ وحفصٌ ﴿كَما يَقُولُونَ﴾ بالياء من تحت، والجمهورُ بالتاء. ومعنى ﴿لابْتَغَوْا إلى ذِي العَرْشِ سَبِيلًا﴾: إلى مغالبته وإفسادِ ملكه؛ لأنهم شركاؤه كما يفعل الملوكُ بعضُهم مع بعضٍ، وقال هذا المعنى أو مثلَه ابنُ جُبيرٍ وأبو عليٍّ الفارسيُّ والنقّاشُ والمتكلِّمون، أبو منصورٍ وغيرُه، وعلى هذا تكون الآيةُ بيانًا للتمانُع، كما في قوله: ﴿لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إلّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا﴾ [الأنبياء: 22]، ويأتي تفسيرُها إن شاء الله تعالى.

وقال قتادةُ ما معناه: لابتغَوْا إلى التقرّبِ إلى ذي العرش والزُّلفى لديه، وكانوا يقولون: إنّ الأصنامَ تُقرِّبهم إلى الله، فإذا علموا أنها تحتاج إلى الله فقد بطل كونُها آلهةً، ويكون كقوله: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إلى رَبِّهِمُ الوَسِيلَةَ أيُّهم أقْرَبُ﴾ [الإسراء: 57]. والكافُ من (كما) في موضعِ نصبٍ.

وقال الحوفي: متعلقةٌ بما تعلّقت به (مَعَ)، وهو الاستقرارُ، و(مَعَهُ) خبرُ كان.

وقال أبو البقاء: كَوْنًا لقولِكم.

وقال الزمخشري: و(إذًا) دالّةٌ على أنّ ما بعدها، وهو (لابتغَوْا)، جوابٌ عن مقالةِ المشركين وجزاءٌ لـ(لو). انتهى. وعُطِف (وتعالى) على قوله: (سبحانَه)؛ لأنه اسمٌ قام مقامَ المصدرِ الذي هو في معنى الفعل، أي: براءةَ الله، وقُدِّر تنزَّهَ، و(تعالى) يتعلّق به على سبيل الإعمال، إذ يصحّ لـ(سبحانَ) أن يتعلّق به (عن) كما في قوله: ﴿سُبْحانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ العِزَّةِ عَمّا يَصِفُونَ﴾ [الصافات: 180]، والتعالي في حقّه تعالى هو بالمكانةِ لا بالمكانِ. وقرأ الأخَوانِ: «عمّا تقولون» بالتاء من فوق، وباقي السبعة بالياء. وانتصب (عُلُوًّا) على أنه مصدرٌ على غير الصدر، أي: تعاليًا، ووُصف بـ(كبيرًا) مبالغةً في معنى البراءةِ والبُعدِ عمّا وصفوه به؛ لأنّ المنافاةَ بين الواجبِ لذاتِه والممكنِ لذاتِه، وبين القديمِ والمحدَثِ، وبين الغنيِّ والمحتاجِ منافاةٌ لا تقبل الزيادةَ.

ونسبةُ التسبيح للسماوات والأرض ومَن فيهنّ من مَلَكٍ وإنسٍ وجنٍّ حملَه بعضُهم على النطقِ بالتسبيح حقيقةً، وأنّ ما لا حياةَ فيه ولا نُموَّ يُحدِث الله له نطقًا، وهذا هو ظاهرُ اللفظ، ولذلك جاء ﴿ولَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾. وقال بعضُهم: ما كان من نامٍ حيوانٍ وغيرِه يُسبّح حقيقةً، وبه قال عكرمةُ، قال: الشجرةُ تُسبّح والأُسطوانةُ لا تُسبّح.

وسُئل الحسنُ عن الخِوان: أيُسبّح؟ فقال: قد كان يُسبّح مرةً، يشير إلى أنه حين كان شجرةً كان يسبّح، وحين صار خِوانًا مدهونًا صار جمادًا لا يسبّح. وقيل: التسبيحُ المنسوبُ لما لا يعقل مجازٌ، ومعناه: أنها تسبّح بلسانِ الحال، حيث يدلّ على الصانع وعلى قدرتِه وحكمتِه وكمالِه، فكأنها تنطق بذلك، وكأنها تُنزّه اللهَ عمّا لا يجوز عليه من الشركاء وغيرِها. ويكون قولُه: ﴿ولَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾ (p-41) خطابًا للمشركين، وهم وإن كانوا معترفين بالخالق أنه الله، لكنهم لمّا جعلوا معه آلهةً لم ينظروا ولم يُقِرّوا؛ لأنّ نتيجةَ النظرِ الصحيحِ والإقرارِ الثابتِ خلافُ ما كانوا عليه، فإذا لم يفقهوا التسبيحَ ولم يستوضحوا الدلالةَ على الخالق، فيكون التسبيحُ المسنَدُ إلى السماوات والأرض ومَن فيهنّ على سبيل المجاز قدرًا مشتركًا بين الجميع، وإن كان يصدر التسبيحُ حقيقةً ممّن فيهنّ من مَلَكٍ وإنسٍ وجانٍّ، ولا يُحمل نسبتُه إلى السماوات والأرض على المجاز، ونسبتُه إلى الملائكة والثَّقَلَين على الحقيقة؛ لئلّا يكون جمعًا بين المجاز والحقيقة بلفظٍ واحدٍ.

وقال ابن عطية: ثم أعاد على السماوات والأرض ضميرَ مَن يعقل لمّا أسند إليها فعلَ العاقل، وهو التسبيح. انتهى. ويُعنى بالضمير في قوله: ﴿ومَن فِيهِنَّ﴾، وكأنه تُخيّل أنّ (هُنّ) لا يكون إلا لمن يعقل من المؤنثات، وليس كما تُخيّل، بل (هُنّ) يكون ضميرَ الجمعِ المؤنثِ مطلقًا. وقرأ النحويّان وحمزةُ وحفصٌ: ﴿تُسَبِّحُ﴾ بالتاء من فوق، وباقي السبعة بالياء، وفي بعض المصاحف «سَبَّحَتْ» له السماواتُ بلفظ الماضي وتاءِ التأنيث، وهي قراءةُ عبدِ الله والأعمشِ وطلحةَ بنِ مُصرِّفٍ.

﴿إنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيمًا﴾ حيث لا يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على سوءِ نظرِكم ﴿غَفُورًا﴾ إن رجعتم ووحّدتم الله تعالى.

[p. 33] When God the Exalted forbade the killing of children, He forbade bringing about their existence through unlawful means. So He forbade approaching adultery (zina), and this entails the prohibition of adultery itself. Zina is mostly pronounced with a short vowel (qasr), but it may also be pronounced with a long vowel (mad), which is linguistically permissible and not a poetic necessity. This is how the lexicographers have transmitted it. An example of the long form is the verse of the poet, who is al-Farazdaq:

*Abu Hadir, whoever commits zina will be known for his zina,*
*and whoever drinks the intoxicant will wake up intoxicated.*

It is also narrated as "Abu Khalid." Another poet said:

*It was an obligation, as you say, just as*
*zina was an obligation punished by stoning.*

The meaning of "lam yazal" is "he did not cease," that is, it did not cease to be *fahisha*, a disobedience that is *fahisha*, meaning abominable and increasing in abomination. ﴿And evil is the way﴾, that is, the way of it is wicked, because it is a path that leads to the Fire. Ibn Atiyyah said: "*sabilan* is in the accusative as a tamyiz (accusative of specification), the implied meaning being: 'and evil is its way.'" End quote. If *sabilan* is in the accusative as a tamyiz, then it is a specification of the hidden pronoun within *sa'a* (evil is). This is among the pronouns explained by what follows it, and the object of the blame is omitted. In that case, the implied meaning cannot be "and evil is its way, a way," because then its subject would not be a pronoun referring to the genus, explained by the tamyiz. The implied meaning would also remain without the object of the blame. The explanation of God's words ﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾ has already been given at the end of al-An'am. Al-Dahhak said: "This is the first thing revealed in the Qur'an concerning killing." End quote.

When He forbade the killing of children and their creation through unlawful means, He forbade the killing of a soul. He moved from the specific to the general. The apparent meaning is that all of these are independent prohibitions, not included under His words ﴿And your Lord has decreed﴾ [al-Isra: 23], as the prohibition of "that you worship none but Him" is included under it. ﴿Wronged﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) from the hidden pronoun in *qutila* (was killed), and the meaning is: he was killed without right. ﴿We have given his heir﴾, who is the one who legally seeks retaliation for his blood. According to Abu Hanifah and his companions, men, women, and children who inherit are included in "heir," in proportion to their shares of inheritance, because the heir in their view is the inheritor here. Malik said: "Women have no share at all in retaliation (qisas); retaliation belongs only to men." From Ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Hakam: "Women have no part at all in pardoning or in the blood-wit (diyah), and the ruler (sultan) has the authority to act against the killer, either by carrying out retaliation against him or by establishing proof against him." This was reported by al-Zamakhshari. Ibn Atiyyah said: "*Sultan* means proof, and also the king who has been granted the choice between accepting blood-money or pardoning." This was reported by Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak. Qatadah said: "*Sultan* is retaliation (qawad)." In the book *al-Tahrir*: "*Sultan* means power and authority." Ibn Abbas said: "It is the evidence in seeking retaliation." Al-Hasan said: "Retaliation." Mujahid said: "The proof." Ibn Zayd said: "The governor, meaning a governor who gives him justice in his right."

The apparent reference of the pronoun in ﴿so let him not exceed bounds in killing﴾ is to the heir. The excess that is forbidden is that he kill someone other than the killer, as Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said; or that he kill two people in exchange for one, as Ibn Jubayr said; or that he kill someone more noble than the one who was killed, as Ibn Zayd said; or that he mutilate, as Qatadah said; or that the killer act without the ruler, as al-Zajjaj mentioned.

Abu Abdullah al-Razi said: "The authority (*al-saltanah*) is general and is explained by God's words ﴿Retaliation is prescribed for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178], and so on. This is also indicated by the fact that the heir is given the choice between retaliation and blood-money. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said on the day of the conquest: 'Whoever kills a person, his family has a choice between two options: if they wish, they may kill; and if they wish, they may take the blood-money.'" So the meaning of ﴿let him not exceed bounds in killing﴾ is: let him not proceed to carry out the killing, and let him be content with taking the blood-money or lean toward pardon. The word *fi* is taken to mean *bi* (with), so that the meaning is: he does not become an transgressor by reason of his proceeding to kill. Its meaning is an encouragement to pardon, as He said: ﴿And that you pardon is nearer to righteousness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237]. End quote, summarized. Even if it is granted that *fi* means *bi*, the meaning would not be sound, because one who kills the killer of his relative in accordance with right does not become an excessive killer by killing him. The apparent meaning, and God knows best, is the prohibition of what the pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah used to do: killing a group for one person, killing someone other than the killer, mutilation, and retaliating against the one who killed him by killing in turn. Muhalhil, when he killed Bujayr ibn al-Harith ibn Abbad, said: "Pay with the sandal-strap of Kulayb."

Those who went furthest in claiming that the pronoun in ﴿let him not exceed bounds﴾ does not refer to the heir, but refers to the agent implied by ﴿and whoever is killed﴾, meaning: let him not exceed bounds in killing by aggression and injustice, so that he kills someone whom he has no right to kill, were mistaken. [p. 34] The majority read ﴿let him not exceed﴾ with the third-person *ya*. The two brothers, Zayd ibn Ali, Hudhayfah, Ibn Thabbat, al-A'mash, Mujahid in one report, and a group read it with the second-person *ta*, as found in a copy of Ibn Atiyyah's tafsir, and Ibn Amir. This is an error. The apparent meaning is that it is addressed to the heir, so the pronoun refers to him. Al-Tabari said: "The address is to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and to the imams after him, meaning: do not kill anyone other than the killer." End quote. Ibn Atiyyah said: "Abu Muslim al-Sarraj, the companion of the Abbasid movement, read it so." Al-Zamakhshari said: "Abu Muslim, the companion of the dynasty, read it so." The author of *Kitab al-Lawami'* or Muslim al-Ijli, client of the companion of the dynasty, read ﴿fa-la yusrif﴾ with a *damma* on the *fa*, as a statement, and its meaning is a prohibition, since commands and prohibitions may come in the form of statements. Ibn Atiyyah, in arguing against Abu Muslim, said: "There is an issue with the reading. In the reading of Ubayy, 'so do not exceed bounds in killing' — that the guardian of the one killed was helped." End quote. He refuted it on the basis of "and do not kill." The better course is to take his words "that the guardian of the one killed" as an explanation, not as a reading, because it contradicts the written text, and because what is well attested from him is ﴿indeed he was helped﴾, like the reading of the majority. The pronoun in *innahu* refers to the heir, for consistency of pronouns. His help consists of God making retaliation obligatory for him, so nothing more is added to that; or his help is through the assistance of the ruler and the believers' support in obtaining the right. It has also been said that the pronoun refers to the one who was killed: God helped him by making retaliation obligatory upon his killing in this world, and helped him with reward in the Hereafter. Ibn Atiyyah said: "This is the stronger view, because he is the one wronged, and the word 'help' accompanies wrong, as in his peace be upon him words: 'and helping the wronged and fulfilling the oath,' and his words: 'Help your brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed,' along with many other examples." It has also been said that it refers to the killing. Abu Ubayd said that it refers to the killer, because if he is killed in this world and thereby saved from the punishment of the Hereafter, then he has been helped. This is weak and remote in purpose. Al-Zamakhshari said: "He means that the pronoun in *innahu* refers to the one whom the guardian kills without right, and who is excessively killed. He is helped by making retaliation obligatory upon the transgressor." End quote. This is very remote.

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best, until he reaches his maturity﴾. When He forbade the destruction of souls, He forbade taking wealth, as He said: "Your blood, your property, and your honor are forbidden to you." Since the orphan is weak and unable to defend his property because of his youth, He specifically forbade approaching his property. The explanation of this verse was given earlier at the end of al-An'am.

﴿And fulfill the covenant﴾ is general to what a person contracts between himself and his Lord, or between himself and a human being, in obedience. ﴿Indeed the covenant was ever questioned﴾. The apparent meaning is that the covenant itself is what is questioned of the one who made it, to fulfill it and not break it or waste it. Or it may be a figure of speech, as if it were said to the covenant: "Why were you broken?" It is personified as if it were a being that is asked why it was broken, indicating its obedience to the breaking and the consequences that follow from breaking it, just as in His words: ﴿And when the buried girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾ [al-Takwir: 8], according to the reading with the *lam* silent and the *ta* of address with a kasra. It has also been said that there is an omitted modifier, meaning: indeed the one who made the covenant will be questioned about it if he does not fulfill it.

Then He commanded the fulfillment of measure and the use of the straight balance, which pertains to dealings in wealth. In His words ﴿And fulfill the measure﴾ there is an indication that the measuring is the seller's duty, because that is not said to the buyer. Al-Hasan said: "*Al-qistas* is the steelyard, which is the *filastun*, also called *qarastun*." Mujahid said: "*Al-qistas* is justice, not an instrument." The two brothers and Hafs read it with a kasra on the *qaf*; the rest of the seven read it with a damma. Both are dialectal forms. A group read with substitution of the first *sin* by a *sad*. Ibn Atiyyah said: "The word is for emphasis, derived from *qist* (justice)." End quote. It is not possible that it derives from *qist*, because the roots differ: *qist* has the root q-s-t, while this has q-s-t-s, unless one posits that the *sin* at the end is an added letter, like the *sin* in *qudmus*, *dughbus*, and *urfas*. That is possible, but it is not one of the recognized positions for the addition of *sin*. The restriction with His words ﴿when you measure﴾ means: at the time of your measuring, as an emphasis, and so that the fulfillment is not delayed by giving less and then making up the difference later. Thus the fulfillment does not lag behind the time of measuring.

﴿That is better﴾, that is, the fulfillment and the weighing, because in it hearts are made content through being characterized by justice and by delivering what is right. ﴿And better in outcome﴾, that is, in its end, since no burden of responsibility remains on the one who fulfills and weighs, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. *Ta'wil* comes from *ma'al*, which means the return, as in His words: "better in return, better in reward, better in hope." Its outcome is better because he is known for guarding against fraud, so people rely on him in transactions, and hearts are inclined toward him.

﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge; indeed the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned﴾. ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, nor will you reach the mountains in height. All that — its evil is ever hateful in the sight of your Lord. That is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. And do not make with God another deity, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished.﴾

When He commanded three things — the fulfillment of the covenant, the fulfillment of measure, and weighing with the straight balance — He followed them with three prohibitions: "and do not pursue," "and do not walk," and "and do not make." The meaning of "*wa la taqfu*" (and do not pursue) is: do not follow what you have no knowledge of, whether in speech or action. He forbade us to say what we do not know and to act upon what we do not know. This includes the prohibition of blind following (taqlid), because it is following without knowing its soundness. Ibn Abbas said: "Its meaning: do not accuse anyone of what you do not know." Qatadah said: "Do not say: 'I saw' when you did not see, 'I heard' when you did not hear, and 'I knew' when you did not know." Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "Do not bear false witness." Ibn Atiyyah said: "This word is used for slander and defamation." End quote. In a hadith: "Whoever accuses a believer of what is not in him, God will confine him in the mire of ruin (radghat al-khabal) until he produces the way out." In another hadith: "We are the sons of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah; you do not accuse us, nor do we disown our father." From this is the saying of al-Nabighah al-Ja'di:

*Like statues, noble of nose, sitting still, the rain-clouds' sweetness among them, they do not follow the accusations.*

And al-Kumayt said:

*I do not strike the innocent without a crime, nor do I accuse the nurses if they are accused.*

Here is the translation of the passage.

The gist of this is that He forbade following what one has no knowledge of, and this is a universal principle under which many categories fall. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Those who oppose ijtihad have used this as evidence, but it is not valid, because that (conjecture) is a kind of knowledge, and the Sharia has established predominant opinion (ghalib al-zann) in the place of knowledge and commanded acting upon it." End of quotation.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿ولا تَقْفُ﴾ with the waw elided, as a jussive of qafa (تَقْفُ, from qafa, "to follow"). Zayd ibn 'Ali read "ولا تَقْفُو" with the waw retained, as the poet said:

"You satirized Zabban, then came apologizing / for the satire of Zabban; you did not satirize and you did not leave off."

Retaining the waw, the ya', and the alif with the jussive is a dialectal usage among some Arabs and a poetic necessity for others.

Mu'adh al-Qari read ﴿ولا تَقْفُ﴾ on the pattern of تَقُلْ, from qaafa yaqoofu. The Arabs say: "quftu atharahu" and "qafawtu atharahu" (I followed his track), and both are two dialects, given the existence of their derivational forms, like jabadha and jadhaba. Qa'a al-jamalu al-naqata and qa'aha (the camel mounted the she-camel) when he mounted her. Qaf is not a metathesis of qafa, as the author of al-Lawami' allowed.

Al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿والفُؤادَ﴾ with a fatha on the fa' and waw: the hamza was changed to waw after the damma in al-fu'ad, and then the heart was retained with the fatha. It is a dialect of ﴿الفُؤادُ﴾ [al-Najm: 11]. Abu Hatim and others rejected it. Moreover, it does not attach to a verb ('alam), because its complement would precede it.

Al-Hawfi said: it is attached to what (li-ka) is attached to, namely the stable predicate (al-istiqrar), and this is not apparent. In His saying ﴿إنَّ السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ there is evidence that knowledge is derived from the senses and from the intellects. This came in the Qur'anic order: beginning with hearing, then sight, then the heart.

(Ula'ika) is a demonstrative for "those" referring to ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾, and it is a demonstrative for the masculine and feminine plural, rational and non-rational alike. Ibn 'Atiyya imagined that it is restricted to the rational, saying: "He expressed ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ with ula'ika because they are senses that perceive, and He made them accountable in this verse, so they are in the state of one who reasons, and for this reason He expressed them with ula'ika."

Sibawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, in His saying ﴿رَأيْتُهم لِي ساجِدِينَ﴾ [Yusuf: 4] said: he said "ra'aytuhum" regarding the stars, because He described them with prostration, which is an act of one who reasons, so He expressed them with the pronoun of one who reasons. Al-Zajjaj related that the Arabs express both those who reason and those who do not with ula'ika, and he and al-Tabari recited:

"He blamed the dwellings after the abode of al-Liwa, / and life after those days."

As for Abu Ishaq's report about the language, it is a matter to be withheld. As for the verse, the narration in it is "al-aqwam" (the peoples). End of quotation.

What he imagined is not correct. The grammarians recite it as "ba'da ula'ika al-ayyam," and they would not recite except what was transmitted. The use of ula', ula, ula'ika and ulalika for what does not reason is not known to have any disagreement.

(Kull) is a subject, and the sentence is its predicate. The subject of (kana) returns to (kull), and likewise the pronoun in ﴿مَسْئُولًا﴾. The pronoun in (anhu) returns to "ma" in His saying ﴿ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾, so the meaning is that each of ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ will be questioned about what one has no knowledge of, that is, about the absence of what one has no knowledge of. This is the apparent meaning.

Al-Zajjaj said: they are called as witnesses, as He said: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ ألْسِنَتُهم وأيْدِيهِمْ وأرْجُلُهُمْ﴾ [al-Nur: 24]. Al-Qurtubi said in his Ahkam: the heart is questioned about what it believed, the hearing about what it heard, and the sight about what it saw.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: Allah the Exalted questions a person's hearing, sight and heart about what he said that he had no knowledge of, so his denial comes from his own limbs, and that is the utmost disgrace.

It was said: the pronoun in (kana) and ﴿مَسْئُولًا﴾ refer to the one who follows what he has no knowledge of, and the pronoun in (anhu) refers to (kull). Thus this is an iltifat (shift), since if it were in the second person, the construction would be "kullu ula'ika kunta 'anhu mas'ula."

Al-Zamakhshari said: "anhu" is in the place of the nominative as the agent, meaning each one of them was questioned about it, so "mas'ul" is attributed to the prepositional phrase, like "al-maghdub" in His saying ﴿غَيْرِ المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Fatiha: 7]. It is said to a person: why did you hear what it was not permissible for you to hear? Why did you look at what it was not permissible for you to look at? Why did you resolve upon what it was not permissible for you to resolve upon? End of quotation.

What he went to, that "anhu" is in the place of the nominative as agent, and by this he means that it is a non-named object, is not permissible. This is because the prepositional phrase and what takes the place of the agent, whether a direct object, a verbal noun or an adverbial, under their conditions, function as the agent. Just as the agent may not be fronted, so too what functions like it and takes its place. So when you say "ghadiba 'ala Zayd," it is not permissible to say "'ala Zayd ghadiba," unlike "ghadibtu 'ala Zayd," where "'ala Zayd ghadibtu" is permissible. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas has related the consensus of the grammarians that a prepositional phrase that takes the place of the agent may not be fronted before the verb. He mentioned this in his book al-Muqni'. So ﴿عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا﴾ is not like ﴿المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, because in ﴿عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا﴾ the prepositional phrase is fronted, while in ﴿المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ it is delayed. Al-Zamakhshari's statement "wa lima nazarta ma lam yahill laka" omitted "ila," and this is not permissible except in poetic necessity, since "nazara" is transitive with "ila," so the construction should have been "wa lima nazarta ila ma lam yahill laka," as he said "al-nazar ilayhi," thus transitive with "ila."

(Maraḥan) is accusative as a circumstantial state, meaning "marihan" (exulting), as you say "ja'a Zayd rakdan," meaning "rakidan" (running). Or it is accusative by eliding a modifier, meaning "dha maraḥ" (possessed of exultation). Some allowed that it be an object of purpose: "wa la tamshi fi al-ard limaraḥ" (do not walk on the earth for exultation). This does not appear. It has preceded that maraḥ is joy and exhilaration in ease and happiness, and it seems it was implicitly given the meaning of arrogance (al-ikhtiyal), because the predominance of joy and happiness is accompanied by haughtiness and arrogance. For this reason it is given as the cause by His saying ﴿إنَّكَ لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الأرْضَ﴾.

A group, as transmitted by Ya'qub, read "maraḥan" with a kasra on the ra', and it is a state: do not walk arrogant and haughty. Mujahid said: "You will not tear the earth with your walking on your heels in pride and luxury, and you will not reach the mountains" with walking on the fronts of your feet in boasting. (Tulan) — the interpretation is that your power does not reach this extent, so that would be a means to arrogance. Al-Zajjaj said: "Do not walk on the earth" arrogant, boastful, and its counterpart is ﴿وعِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلى الأرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾ [al-Furqan: 63] and ﴿اقْصِدْ في مَشْيِكَ﴾ [Luqman: 19], and ﴿ولا تَمْشِ في الأرْضِ مَرَحًا إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ﴾ [Luqman: 18].

Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الأرْضَ﴾ means you will not make a rent in it by your treading on it and the severity of your stamping, ﴿ولَنْ تَبْلُغَ الجِبالَ طُولًا﴾ by your stretching yourself, and this is a mockery of the arrogant.

Al-Jarrah al-A'rabi read "﴿لَنْ تَخْرِقَ﴾" with a damma on the ra'. Abu Hatim said: this dialect is not known. It was said: by this is indicated that man is confined between two inanimate things, weak in affecting them by tearing or reaching height, and whoever is in this position is not fit for arrogance.

The poet said:

"Do not walk above the earth except in humility, / for beneath it are people who are higher than you."

The better parsing of His saying ﴿طُولًا﴾ is as a specification (tamyiz), meaning your height will not reach the mountains. Al-Hawfi said: ﴿طُولًا﴾ is accusative as a circumstantial state, and the agent of the state is (tabluga), and it may be that the agent is (takhraqa), and ﴿طُولًا﴾ means "mutatawil" (stretching). End of quotation.

Abu al-Baqa said: ﴿طُولًا﴾ is a verbal noun in the place of a state from the subject or the object, and it may be a specification, an object of purpose, and a verbal noun from the meaning of (tabluga). End of quotation.

The two Haramis (Ibn Kathir and Nafi' — Meccan and Medinan), Abu 'Amr, Abu Ja'far and al-A'raj read "sayyi'atan" in the accusative and feminine. The rest of the Seven, and al-Hasan and Masruq, read ﴿سَيِّئُهُ﴾ with a damma on the hamza, as a construct with the masculine third-person pronoun. 'Abd Allah read "sayyi'atuhu" in the plural as a construct with the pronoun, and also from him "sayyi'at" without it, and also from him "kana khabithuhu."

As for the first reading, the apparent meaning is that this refers to the verbal nouns of the two prohibitions preceding, namely following what one has no knowledge of, and walking on the earth exultantly. It was said: it refers to all the prohibitions mentioned earlier in this sura. "Sayyi'atan" is the predicate of kana and is feminine; then He said "makruhan," which is masculine. Al-Zamakhshari said: sayyi'a in the category of nouns is like dhanb (sin), and the noun has lost the rule of adjectives, so no account is taken of its feminine form, and there is no difference between one who reads "sayyi'atan" and one who reads "sayyi'an." Do you not see that you say "al-zina sayyi'a" just as you say "al-sariqa sayyi'a," so you do not distinguish in attributing it to masculine or feminine. End of quotation. And this is a good explanation.

It was said: "makruhan" was mentioned according to the wording of (kull). They permitted that "makruhan" be a second predicate of kana according to the view of one who permits multiple predicates of kana, and that it be an apposition to sayyi'a, though apposition with a derived noun is weak, and that it be a state from the pronoun concealed in the adverbial preceding it, the adverbial being in the place of a qualifier. It was said: it is also permissible that it be an attribute of sayyi'a: since its feminine is metaphorical, it may be described by a masculine. This was deemed weak, because the permissibility of this is only when the verb with a metaphorical feminine subject precedes; when it follows and is attributed to its pronoun, it is ugly. You say "abqala al-ardu iblalaha" (the earth sprouted its vegetation), which is eloquent, but "al-ardu abqala" is ugly.

As for one who reads "sayyi'uhu" with the masculine and the construct, then "sayyi'uhu" is the subject of kana and "makruhan" is the predicate. Since among the attributes mentioned there are both bad and good, He pointed to the whole with "dhalika," and He used the singular "sayyi'a," which is what is forbidden, so the judgment of disapproval applies to it from His saying "la taj'al" to the end of the prohibitions.

As for the reading of 'Abd Allah, it is parsed as a case in which the plural is predicated with a singular masculine, which is rare, like His saying:

"Fa inna al-hawadith awda biha"
(since misfortunes have destroyed them),

because "al-hidthan" is permissible in place of "al-hawadith." Similarly here, "kana ma yasu'u" (what displeases) stands in place of its bad deeds. That (dhalika) refers to all kinds of obligations from His saying ﴿لا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إلَهًا آخَرَ﴾ [al-Isra: 22] to His saying ﴿ولا تَمْشِ في الأرْضِ مَرَحًا﴾, and they are twenty-four types of obligations, some of them commands and some prohibitions, beginning with His saying ﴿لا تَجْعَلْ﴾ [al-Isra: 22]. He concluded the verses with His saying ﴿ولا تَجْعَلْ﴾ and said "mimma awha" (of what He revealed), because that is part of what was revealed to him, since other obligations were revealed to him. ﴿مِمّا أوْحى﴾ is a predicate of that. ﴿مِنَ الحِكْمَةِ﴾ may be attached to "awha," may be an apposition to "ma," or may be a state from the accusative pronoun elided that returns to "ma." These obligations are wisdom, because their sum returns to the command of monotheism, the various acts of obedience, turning away from the world and turning toward the Hereafter; reason indicates their soundness, and they are laws in all religions that do not admit abrogation (naskh).

From Ibn 'Abbas: these verses were on the tablets of Moses, peace be upon him, the first of which is ﴿لا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إلَهًا آخَرَ﴾ [al-Isra: 22]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وكَتَبْنا لَهُ في الألْواحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-A'raf: 145]. And Allah the Exalted repeated the prohibition of association; in the first prohibition...

﴿فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَخْذُولًا﴾ [الإسراء: 22]. وفي الثاني: ﴿فَتُلْقى في جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَدْحُورًا﴾. والفرق بين «مذمومٍ» و«ملومٍ» أنّ كونه مذمومًا هو أن يُذكر أنّ الفعل الذي أقدم عليه قبيحٌ مُنكَرٌ، وكونه ملومًا هو أن يُقال له بعد الفعل والذمّ: لِمَ فعلتَ كذا؟ وما حملك عليه؟ وما استفدتَ منه إلّا إلحاقَ الضررِ بنفسك؟ فأوّلُ الأمر الذمُّ وآخرُه اللومُ. والفرق بين «مخذولٍ» و«مدحورٍ» أنّ المخذول هو المتروكُ إعانتُه ونصرُه والمفوَّضُ إلى (p-39) نفسِه، والمدحورُ المطرودُ المُبعَدُ على سبيل الإهانة له والاستخفاف به، فأوّلُ الأمر الخِذلان وآخرُه الطردُ مُهانًا. وكان وصفُ الذمّ والخِذلان يكون في الدنيا، ووصفُ اللوم والدُّحور يكون في الآخرة، ولذلك جاء ﴿فَتُلْقى في جَهَنَّمَ﴾. والخطابُ بالنهي في هذه الآيات للسامع غيرِ الرسول.

وقال الزمخشري: ولقد جعل الله ‑ عزّ وعلا ‑ فاتحتَها وخاتمتَها النهيَ عن الشرك؛ لأنّ التوحيدَ هو رأسُ كلِّ حكمةٍ وملاكُها، ومَن عَدِمه لم تنفعْه حِكَمُه وعلومُه وإن بذّ فيها الحكماءَ وحكّ بيافوخِه السماءَ، وما أغنتْ عن الفلاسفةِ أسفارُ الحِكَم وهم عن دين الله أضلُّ من النَّعَم.

﴿أفَأصْفاكم رَبُّكم بِالبَنِينَ واتَّخَذَ مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ إناثًا إنَّكم لَتَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا عَظِيمًا﴾ ﴿ولَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا في هَذا القُرْآنِ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا وما يَزِيدُهم إلّا نُفُورًا﴾ ﴿قُلْ لَوْ كانَ مَعَهُ آلِهَةٌ كَما يَقُولُونَ إذًا لابْتَغَوْا إلى ذِي العَرْشِ سَبِيلًا﴾ ﴿سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى عَمّا يَقُولُونَ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ ﴿تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّماواتُ السَّبْعُ والأرْضُ ومَن فِيهِنَّ وإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ ولَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهم إنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا﴾.

لمّا نبّه تعالى على فساد مَن أثبت لله شريكًا ونظيرًا، أتبعه بفساد طريقة مَن أثبت لله ولدًا. والاستفهامُ معناه الإنكارُ والتوبيخ، والخطابُ لِمَن اعتقد أنّ الملائكةَ بناتُ الله. ومعنى ﴿أفَأصْفاكم﴾ آثركم وخصّكم، وهذا كما قال: ﴿ألَهُ البَناتُ ولَكُمُ البَنُونَ﴾ [الطور: 39]، ﴿ألَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ ولَهُ الأُنْثى﴾ [النجم: 21]. وهذا خلافُ الحكمةِ وما عليه معقولُكم وعادتُكم، فإنّ العبيدَ لا يُؤْثَرون بأجودِ الأشياء وأصفاها من الشَّوب، ويكون أرداها وأدونها للسادات. ومعنى ﴿عَظِيمًا﴾ مُبالغًا في المنكر والقبح، حيث أضفتم إليه الأولاد، ثم حيث فضّلتم عليه تعالى أنفسَكم فجعلتم له ما تكرهون، ثم نسبةُ الملائكةِ الذين هم من شريفِ ما خلق إلى الأنوثة.

ومعنى ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ نوّعنا من جهةٍ إلى جهةٍ ومن مثالٍ إلى مثالٍ، والتصريفُ لغةً: صرفُ الشيءِ من جهةٍ إلى جهةٍ، ثم صار كنايةً عن التبيين. وقرأ الجمهور ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ بتشديد الراء. فقال: لم نجعلْه نوعًا واحدًا، بل وعدًا ووعيدًا، ومحكَمًا ومتشابهًا، وأمرًا ونهيًا، وناسخًا ومنسوخًا (نَسْخ: رفعُ حكمٍ شرعيٍّ بدليلٍ متأخرٍ)، وأخبارًا وأمثالًا، مثلَ تصريفِ الرياحِ من صَبًا ودَبورٍ وجَنوبٍ وشَمالٍ. ومفعولُ ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ على هذا المعنى محذوفٌ، وهي هذه الأشياءُ، أي: صرّفنا الأمثالَ والعِبَرَ والحِكَمَ والأحكامَ والأعلامَ. وقيل: المعنى لم نُنزِلْه مرةً واحدةً بل نجومًا، ومعناه: أكثرنا صرفَ جبريلَ إليك، والمفعولُ محذوفٌ، أي: صرّفنا جبريلَ.

وقيل: (في) زائدةٌ، أي: صرّفنا هذا القرآنَ، كما قال: ﴿وأصْلِحْ لِي في ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ [الأحقاف: 15]. وهذا ضعيفٌ؛ لأنّ «في» لا تُزاد. وقال الزمخشري: يجوز أن يريد بهذا القرآنِ إبطالَ إضافتِهم إلى الله البناتِ؛ لأنه مما صرّفه وكرّر ذكره، والمعنى: ولقد (p-40) صرّفنا القولَ في هذا المعنى، وأوقعنا التصريفَ فيه وجعلناه مكانًا للتكرير، ويجوز أن يشير بهذا (القرآنِ) إلى التنزيل، ويريد: ولقد صرّفناه، يعني هذا المعنى في مواضعَ من التنزيل، فترك الضميرَ لأنه معلومٌ. انتهى. فجعل التصريفَ خاصًّا بما دلّت عليه الآيةُ قبله، وجعل مفعولَ ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ إمّا القولَ في هذا المعنى أو المعنى، وهو الضميرُ الذي قدّره في صرّفناه، وغيرُه جعل التصريفَ عامًّا في أشياءَ فقدّر ما يشمل ما سيق له ما قبلَه وغيرَه.

وقرأ الحسنُ بتخفيف الراء. فقال صاحبُ اللوامح: هو بمعنى العامّة، يعني بالعامّة: قراءةَ الجمهور، قال: لأنّ فَعَلَ وفَعَّلَ ربما تعاقبا على معنًى واحدٍ. وقال ابن عطية: على معنى صرَفْنا فيه الناسَ إلى الهدى بالدعاء إلى الله.

وقرأ الجمهور ﴿لِيَذَّكَّرُوا﴾ أي: ليتذكّروا من التذكير، أُدغمت التاءُ في الذال. وقرأ الأخَوانِ وطلحةُ وابنُ وثّابٍ والأعمشُ «لِيَذْكُرُوا» بسكون الذال وضمّ الكاف من الذِّكْرِ أو الذُّكْرِ، أي: ليتّعظوا ويعتبروا وينظروا فيما يُحتجّ به عليهم ويطمئنّوا إليه. ﴿وما يَزِيدُهُمْ﴾ أي: التصريفُ ﴿إلّا نُفُورًا﴾ أي: بُعدًا وفرارًا عن الحق، كما قال: ﴿فَزادَتْهم رِجْسًا إلى رِجْسِهِمْ﴾ [التوبة: 125]، وقال: ﴿فَما لَهم عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ [المدثر: 49] ﴿كَأنَّهم حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾ [المدثر: 50]. والنُّفورُ من أوصاف الدوابّ الشديدةِ الشِّماس. ولمّا ذكر تعالى نسبةَ الولد إليهم وردّ عليهم في ذلك، ذكر قولَهم إنه تعالى معه آلهةٌ وردّ عليهم.

وقرأ ابنُ كثيرٍ وحفصٌ ﴿كَما يَقُولُونَ﴾ بالياء من تحت، والجمهورُ بالتاء. ومعنى ﴿لابْتَغَوْا إلى ذِي العَرْشِ سَبِيلًا﴾: إلى مغالبته وإفسادِ ملكه؛ لأنهم شركاؤه كما يفعل الملوكُ بعضُهم مع بعضٍ، وقال هذا المعنى أو مثلَه ابنُ جُبيرٍ وأبو عليٍّ الفارسيُّ والنقّاشُ والمتكلِّمون، أبو منصورٍ وغيرُه، وعلى هذا تكون الآيةُ بيانًا للتمانُع، كما في قوله: ﴿لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إلّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا﴾ [الأنبياء: 22]، ويأتي تفسيرُها إن شاء الله تعالى.

وقال قتادةُ ما معناه: لابتغَوْا إلى التقرّبِ إلى ذي العرش والزُّلفى لديه، وكانوا يقولون: إنّ الأصنامَ تُقرِّبهم إلى الله، فإذا علموا أنها تحتاج إلى الله فقد بطل كونُها آلهةً، ويكون كقوله: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إلى رَبِّهِمُ الوَسِيلَةَ أيُّهم أقْرَبُ﴾ [الإسراء: 57]. والكافُ من (كما) في موضعِ نصبٍ.

وقال الحوفي: متعلقةٌ بما تعلّقت به (مَعَ)، وهو الاستقرارُ، و(مَعَهُ) خبرُ كان.

وقال أبو البقاء: كَوْنًا لقولِكم.

وقال الزمخشري: و(إذًا) دالّةٌ على أنّ ما بعدها، وهو (لابتغَوْا)، جوابٌ عن مقالةِ المشركين وجزاءٌ لـ(لو). انتهى. وعُطِف (وتعالى) على قوله: (سبحانَه)؛ لأنه اسمٌ قام مقامَ المصدرِ الذي هو في معنى الفعل، أي: براءةَ الله، وقُدِّر تنزَّهَ، و(تعالى) يتعلّق به على سبيل الإعمال، إذ يصحّ لـ(سبحانَ) أن يتعلّق به (عن) كما في قوله: ﴿سُبْحانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ العِزَّةِ عَمّا يَصِفُونَ﴾ [الصافات: 180]، والتعالي في حقّه تعالى هو بالمكانةِ لا بالمكانِ. وقرأ الأخَوانِ: «عمّا تقولون» بالتاء من فوق، وباقي السبعة بالياء. وانتصب (عُلُوًّا) على أنه مصدرٌ على غير الصدر، أي: تعاليًا، ووُصف بـ(كبيرًا) مبالغةً في معنى البراءةِ والبُعدِ عمّا وصفوه به؛ لأنّ المنافاةَ بين الواجبِ لذاتِه والممكنِ لذاتِه، وبين القديمِ والمحدَثِ، وبين الغنيِّ والمحتاجِ منافاةٌ لا تقبل الزيادةَ.

ونسبةُ التسبيح للسماوات والأرض ومَن فيهنّ من مَلَكٍ وإنسٍ وجنٍّ حملَه بعضُهم على النطقِ بالتسبيح حقيقةً، وأنّ ما لا حياةَ فيه ولا نُموَّ يُحدِث الله له نطقًا، وهذا هو ظاهرُ اللفظ، ولذلك جاء ﴿ولَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾. وقال بعضُهم: ما كان من نامٍ حيوانٍ وغيرِه يُسبّح حقيقةً، وبه قال عكرمةُ، قال: الشجرةُ تُسبّح والأُسطوانةُ لا تُسبّح.

وسُئل الحسنُ عن الخِوان: أيُسبّح؟ فقال: قد كان يُسبّح مرةً، يشير إلى أنه حين كان شجرةً كان يسبّح، وحين صار خِوانًا مدهونًا صار جمادًا لا يسبّح. وقيل: التسبيحُ المنسوبُ لما لا يعقل مجازٌ، ومعناه: أنها تسبّح بلسانِ الحال، حيث يدلّ على الصانع وعلى قدرتِه وحكمتِه وكمالِه، فكأنها تنطق بذلك، وكأنها تُنزّه اللهَ عمّا لا يجوز عليه من الشركاء وغيرِها. ويكون قولُه: ﴿ولَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾ (p-41) خطابًا للمشركين، وهم وإن كانوا معترفين بالخالق أنه الله، لكنهم لمّا جعلوا معه آلهةً لم ينظروا ولم يُقِرّوا؛ لأنّ نتيجةَ النظرِ الصحيحِ والإقرارِ الثابتِ خلافُ ما كانوا عليه، فإذا لم يفقهوا التسبيحَ ولم يستوضحوا الدلالةَ على الخالق، فيكون التسبيحُ المسنَدُ إلى السماوات والأرض ومَن فيهنّ على سبيل المجاز قدرًا مشتركًا بين الجميع، وإن كان يصدر التسبيحُ حقيقةً ممّن فيهنّ من مَلَكٍ وإنسٍ وجانٍّ، ولا يُحمل نسبتُه إلى السماوات والأرض على المجاز، ونسبتُه إلى الملائكة والثَّقَلَين على الحقيقة؛ لئلّا يكون جمعًا بين المجاز والحقيقة بلفظٍ واحدٍ.

وقال ابن عطية: ثم أعاد على السماوات والأرض ضميرَ مَن يعقل لمّا أسند إليها فعلَ العاقل، وهو التسبيح. انتهى. ويُعنى بالضمير في قوله: ﴿ومَن فِيهِنَّ﴾، وكأنه تُخيّل أنّ (هُنّ) لا يكون إلا لمن يعقل من المؤنثات، وليس كما تُخيّل، بل (هُنّ) يكون ضميرَ الجمعِ المؤنثِ مطلقًا. وقرأ النحويّان وحمزةُ وحفصٌ: ﴿تُسَبِّحُ﴾ بالتاء من فوق، وباقي السبعة بالياء، وفي بعض المصاحف «سَبَّحَتْ» له السماواتُ بلفظ الماضي وتاءِ التأنيث، وهي قراءةُ عبدِ الله والأعمشِ وطلحةَ بنِ مُصرِّفٍ.

﴿إنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيمًا﴾ حيث لا يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على سوءِ نظرِكم ﴿غَفُورًا﴾ إن رجعتم ووحّدتم الله تعالى.

[p. 33] When God the Exalted forbade the killing of children, He forbade bringing about their existence through unlawful means. So He forbade approaching adultery (zina), and this entails the prohibition of adultery itself. Zina is mostly pronounced with a short vowel (qasr), but it may also be pronounced with a long vowel (mad), which is linguistically permissible and not a poetic necessity. This is how the lexicographers have transmitted it. An example of the long form is the verse of the poet, who is al-Farazdaq:

*Abu Hadir, whoever commits zina will be known for his zina,*
*and whoever drinks the intoxicant will wake up intoxicated.*

It is also narrated as "Abu Khalid." Another poet said:

*It was an obligation, as you say, just as*
*zina was an obligation punished by stoning.*

The meaning of "lam yazal" is "he did not cease," that is, it did not cease to be *fahisha*, a disobedience that is *fahisha*, meaning abominable and increasing in abomination. ﴿And evil is the way﴾, that is, the way of it is wicked, because it is a path that leads to the Fire. Ibn Atiyyah said: "*sabilan* is in the accusative as a tamyiz (accusative of specification), the implied meaning being: 'and evil is its way.'" End quote. If *sabilan* is in the accusative as a tamyiz, then it is a specification of the hidden pronoun within *sa'a* (evil is). This is among the pronouns explained by what follows it, and the object of the blame is omitted. In that case, the implied meaning cannot be "and evil is its way, a way," because then its subject would not be a pronoun referring to the genus, explained by the tamyiz. The implied meaning would also remain without the object of the blame. The explanation of God's words ﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾ has already been given at the end of al-An'am. Al-Dahhak said: "This is the first thing revealed in the Qur'an concerning killing." End quote.

When He forbade the killing of children and their creation through unlawful means, He forbade the killing of a soul. He moved from the specific to the general. The apparent meaning is that all of these are independent prohibitions, not included under His words ﴿And your Lord has decreed﴾ [al-Isra: 23], as the prohibition of "that you worship none but Him" is included under it. ﴿Wronged﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) from the hidden pronoun in *qutila* (was killed), and the meaning is: he was killed without right. ﴿We have given his heir﴾, who is the one who legally seeks retaliation for his blood. According to Abu Hanifah and his companions, men, women, and children who inherit are included in "heir," in proportion to their shares of inheritance, because the heir in their view is the inheritor here. Malik said: "Women have no share at all in retaliation (qisas); retaliation belongs only to men." From Ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Hakam: "Women have no part at all in pardoning or in the blood-wit (diyah), and the ruler (sultan) has the authority to act against the killer, either by carrying out retaliation against him or by establishing proof against him." This was reported by al-Zamakhshari. Ibn Atiyyah said: "*Sultan* means proof, and also the king who has been granted the choice between accepting blood-money or pardoning." This was reported by Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak. Qatadah said: "*Sultan* is retaliation (qawad)." In the book *al-Tahrir*: "*Sultan* means power and authority." Ibn Abbas said: "It is the evidence in seeking retaliation." Al-Hasan said: "Retaliation." Mujahid said: "The proof." Ibn Zayd said: "The governor, meaning a governor who gives him justice in his right."

The apparent reference of the pronoun in ﴿so let him not exceed bounds in killing﴾ is to the heir. The excess that is forbidden is that he kill someone other than the killer, as Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said; or that he kill two people in exchange for one, as Ibn Jubayr said; or that he kill someone more noble than the one who was killed, as Ibn Zayd said; or that he mutilate, as Qatadah said; or that the killer act without the ruler, as al-Zajjaj mentioned.

Abu Abdullah al-Razi said: "The authority (*al-saltanah*) is general and is explained by God's words ﴿Retaliation is prescribed for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178], and so on. This is also indicated by the fact that the heir is given the choice between retaliation and blood-money. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said on the day of the conquest: 'Whoever kills a person, his family has a choice between two options: if they wish, they may kill; and if they wish, they may take the blood-money.'" So the meaning of ﴿let him not exceed bounds in killing﴾ is: let him not proceed to carry out the killing, and let him be content with taking the blood-money or lean toward pardon. The word *fi* is taken to mean *bi* (with), so that the meaning is: he does not become an transgressor by reason of his proceeding to kill. Its meaning is an encouragement to pardon, as He said: ﴿And that you pardon is nearer to righteousness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237]. End quote, summarized. Even if it is granted that *fi* means *bi*, the meaning would not be sound, because one who kills the killer of his relative in accordance with right does not become an excessive killer by killing him. The apparent meaning, and God knows best, is the prohibition of what the pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah used to do: killing a group for one person, killing someone other than the killer, mutilation, and retaliating against the one who killed him by killing in turn. Muhalhil, when he killed Bujayr ibn al-Harith ibn Abbad, said: "Pay with the sandal-strap of Kulayb."

Those who went furthest in claiming that the pronoun in ﴿let him not exceed bounds﴾ does not refer to the heir, but refers to the agent implied by ﴿and whoever is killed﴾, meaning: let him not exceed bounds in killing by aggression and injustice, so that he kills someone whom he has no right to kill, were mistaken. [p. 34] The majority read ﴿let him not exceed﴾ with the third-person *ya*. The two brothers, Zayd ibn Ali, Hudhayfah, Ibn Thabbat, al-A'mash, Mujahid in one report, and a group read it with the second-person *ta*, as found in a copy of Ibn Atiyyah's tafsir, and Ibn Amir. This is an error. The apparent meaning is that it is addressed to the heir, so the pronoun refers to him. Al-Tabari said: "The address is to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and to the imams after him, meaning: do not kill anyone other than the killer." End quote. Ibn Atiyyah said: "Abu Muslim al-Sarraj, the companion of the Abbasid movement, read it so." Al-Zamakhshari said: "Abu Muslim, the companion of the dynasty, read it so." The author of *Kitab al-Lawami'* or Muslim al-Ijli, client of the companion of the dynasty, read ﴿fa-la yusrif﴾ with a *damma* on the *fa*, as a statement, and its meaning is a prohibition, since commands and prohibitions may come in the form of statements. Ibn Atiyyah, in arguing against Abu Muslim, said: "There is an issue with the reading. In the reading of Ubayy, 'so do not exceed bounds in killing' — that the guardian of the one killed was helped." End quote. He refuted it on the basis of "and do not kill." The better course is to take his words "that the guardian of the one killed" as an explanation, not as a reading, because it contradicts the written text, and because what is well attested from him is ﴿indeed he was helped﴾, like the reading of the majority. The pronoun in *innahu* refers to the heir, for consistency of pronouns. His help consists of God making retaliation obligatory for him, so nothing more is added to that; or his help is through the assistance of the ruler and the believers' support in obtaining the right. It has also been said that the pronoun refers to the one who was killed: God helped him by making retaliation obligatory upon his killing in this world, and helped him with reward in the Hereafter. Ibn Atiyyah said: "This is the stronger view, because he is the one wronged, and the word 'help' accompanies wrong, as in his peace be upon him words: 'and helping the wronged and fulfilling the oath,' and his words: 'Help your brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed,' along with many other examples." It has also been said that it refers to the killing. Abu Ubayd said that it refers to the killer, because if he is killed in this world and thereby saved from the punishment of the Hereafter, then he has been helped. This is weak and remote in purpose. Al-Zamakhshari said: "He means that the pronoun in *innahu* refers to the one whom the guardian kills without right, and who is excessively killed. He is helped by making retaliation obligatory upon the transgressor." End quote. This is very remote.

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best, until he reaches his maturity﴾. When He forbade the destruction of souls, He forbade taking wealth, as He said: "Your blood, your property, and your honor are forbidden to you." Since the orphan is weak and unable to defend his property because of his youth, He specifically forbade approaching his property. The explanation of this verse was given earlier at the end of al-An'am.

﴿And fulfill the covenant﴾ is general to what a person contracts between himself and his Lord, or between himself and a human being, in obedience. ﴿Indeed the covenant was ever questioned﴾. The apparent meaning is that the covenant itself is what is questioned of the one who made it, to fulfill it and not break it or waste it. Or it may be a figure of speech, as if it were said to the covenant: "Why were you broken?" It is personified as if it were a being that is asked why it was broken, indicating its obedience to the breaking and the consequences that follow from breaking it, just as in His words: ﴿And when the buried girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾ [al-Takwir: 8], according to the reading with the *lam* silent and the *ta* of address with a kasra. It has also been said that there is an omitted modifier, meaning: indeed the one who made the covenant will be questioned about it if he does not fulfill it.

Then He commanded the fulfillment of measure and the use of the straight balance, which pertains to dealings in wealth. In His words ﴿And fulfill the measure﴾ there is an indication that the measuring is the seller's duty, because that is not said to the buyer. Al-Hasan said: "*Al-qistas* is the steelyard, which is the *filastun*, also called *qarastun*." Mujahid said: "*Al-qistas* is justice, not an instrument." The two brothers and Hafs read it with a kasra on the *qaf*; the rest of the seven read it with a damma. Both are dialectal forms. A group read with substitution of the first *sin* by a *sad*. Ibn Atiyyah said: "The word is for emphasis, derived from *qist* (justice)." End quote. It is not possible that it derives from *qist*, because the roots differ: *qist* has the root q-s-t, while this has q-s-t-s, unless one posits that the *sin* at the end is an added letter, like the *sin* in *qudmus*, *dughbus*, and *urfas*. That is possible, but it is not one of the recognized positions for the addition of *sin*. The restriction with His words ﴿when you measure﴾ means: at the time of your measuring, as an emphasis, and so that the fulfillment is not delayed by giving less and then making up the difference later. Thus the fulfillment does not lag behind the time of measuring.

﴿That is better﴾, that is, the fulfillment and the weighing, because in it hearts are made content through being characterized by justice and by delivering what is right. ﴿And better in outcome﴾, that is, in its end, since no burden of responsibility remains on the one who fulfills and weighs, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. *Ta'wil* comes from *ma'al*, which means the return, as in His words: "better in return, better in reward, better in hope." Its outcome is better because he is known for guarding against fraud, so people rely on him in transactions, and hearts are inclined toward him.

﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge; indeed the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned﴾. ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, nor will you reach the mountains in height. All that — its evil is ever hateful in the sight of your Lord. That is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. And do not make with God another deity, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished.﴾

When He commanded three things — the fulfillment of the covenant, the fulfillment of measure, and weighing with the straight balance — He followed them with three prohibitions: "and do not pursue," "and do not walk," and "and do not make." The meaning of "*wa la taqfu*" (and do not pursue) is: do not follow what you have no knowledge of, whether in speech or action. He forbade us to say what we do not know and to act upon what we do not know. This includes the prohibition of blind following (taqlid), because it is following without knowing its soundness. Ibn Abbas said: "Its meaning: do not accuse anyone of what you do not know." Qatadah said: "Do not say: 'I saw' when you did not see, 'I heard' when you did not hear, and 'I knew' when you did not know." Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "Do not bear false witness." Ibn Atiyyah said: "This word is used for slander and defamation." End quote. In a hadith: "Whoever accuses a believer of what is not in him, God will confine him in the mire of ruin (radghat al-khabal) until he produces the way out." In another hadith: "We are the sons of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah; you do not accuse us, nor do we disown our father." From this is the saying of al-Nabighah al-Ja'di:

*Like statues, noble of nose, sitting still, the rain-clouds' sweetness among them, they do not follow the accusations.*

And al-Kumayt said:

*I do not strike the innocent without a crime, nor do I accuse the nurses if they are accused.*

Here is the translation of the passage.

The gist of this is that He forbade following what one has no knowledge of, and this is a universal principle under which many categories fall. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Those who oppose ijtihad have used this as evidence, but it is not valid, because that (conjecture) is a kind of knowledge, and the Sharia has established predominant opinion (ghalib al-zann) in the place of knowledge and commanded acting upon it." End of quotation.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿ولا تَقْفُ﴾ with the waw elided, as a jussive of qafa (تَقْفُ, from qafa, "to follow"). Zayd ibn 'Ali read "ولا تَقْفُو" with the waw retained, as the poet said:

"You satirized Zabban, then came apologizing / for the satire of Zabban; you did not satirize and you did not leave off."

Retaining the waw, the ya', and the alif with the jussive is a dialectal usage among some Arabs and a poetic necessity for others.

Mu'adh al-Qari read ﴿ولا تَقْفُ﴾ on the pattern of تَقُلْ, from qaafa yaqoofu. The Arabs say: "quftu atharahu" and "qafawtu atharahu" (I followed his track), and both are two dialects, given the existence of their derivational forms, like jabadha and jadhaba. Qa'a al-jamalu al-naqata and qa'aha (the camel mounted the she-camel) when he mounted her. Qaf is not a metathesis of qafa, as the author of al-Lawami' allowed.

Al-Jarrah al-'Uqayli read ﴿والفُؤادَ﴾ with a fatha on the fa' and waw: the hamza was changed to waw after the damma in al-fu'ad, and then the heart was retained with the fatha. It is a dialect of ﴿الفُؤادُ﴾ [al-Najm: 11]. Abu Hatim and others rejected it. Moreover, it does not attach to a verb ('alam), because its complement would precede it.

Al-Hawfi said: it is attached to what (li-ka) is attached to, namely the stable predicate (al-istiqrar), and this is not apparent. In His saying ﴿إنَّ السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ there is evidence that knowledge is derived from the senses and from the intellects. This came in the Qur'anic order: beginning with hearing, then sight, then the heart.

(Ula'ika) is a demonstrative for "those" referring to ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾, and it is a demonstrative for the masculine and feminine plural, rational and non-rational alike. Ibn 'Atiyya imagined that it is restricted to the rational, saying: "He expressed ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ with ula'ika because they are senses that perceive, and He made them accountable in this verse, so they are in the state of one who reasons, and for this reason He expressed them with ula'ika."

Sibawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, in His saying ﴿رَأيْتُهم لِي ساجِدِينَ﴾ [Yusuf: 4] said: he said "ra'aytuhum" regarding the stars, because He described them with prostration, which is an act of one who reasons, so He expressed them with the pronoun of one who reasons. Al-Zajjaj related that the Arabs express both those who reason and those who do not with ula'ika, and he and al-Tabari recited:

"He blamed the dwellings after the abode of al-Liwa, / and life after those days."

As for Abu Ishaq's report about the language, it is a matter to be withheld. As for the verse, the narration in it is "al-aqwam" (the peoples). End of quotation.

What he imagined is not correct. The grammarians recite it as "ba'da ula'ika al-ayyam," and they would not recite except what was transmitted. The use of ula', ula, ula'ika and ulalika for what does not reason is not known to have any disagreement.

(Kull) is a subject, and the sentence is its predicate. The subject of (kana) returns to (kull), and likewise the pronoun in ﴿مَسْئُولًا﴾. The pronoun in (anhu) returns to "ma" in His saying ﴿ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾, so the meaning is that each of ﴿السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ will be questioned about what one has no knowledge of, that is, about the absence of what one has no knowledge of. This is the apparent meaning.

Al-Zajjaj said: they are called as witnesses, as He said: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ ألْسِنَتُهم وأيْدِيهِمْ وأرْجُلُهُمْ﴾ [al-Nur: 24]. Al-Qurtubi said in his Ahkam: the heart is questioned about what it believed, the hearing about what it heard, and the sight about what it saw.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: Allah the Exalted questions a person's hearing, sight and heart about what he said that he had no knowledge of, so his denial comes from his own limbs, and that is the utmost disgrace.

It was said: the pronoun in (kana) and ﴿مَسْئُولًا﴾ refer to the one who follows what he has no knowledge of, and the pronoun in (anhu) refers to (kull). Thus this is an iltifat (shift), since if it were in the second person, the construction would be "kullu ula'ika kunta 'anhu mas'ula."

Al-Zamakhshari said: "anhu" is in the place of the nominative as the agent, meaning each one of them was questioned about it, so "mas'ul" is attributed to the prepositional phrase, like "al-maghdub" in His saying ﴿غَيْرِ المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Fatiha: 7].
