The meaning is that every people who expelled their messenger from among them, Allah's sunnah is that He destroys them after his expulsion and uproots them, and they do not remain after him except a little. Al-Farra' said: ﴿سُنَّةَ﴾ is in the accusative by dropping the preposition, because the meaning is "like the sunnah," so it is put in the accusative after the omission of the kaf; and according to this, one does not stop at His saying: ﴿إلّا قَلِيلًا﴾ (Al-Isra': 85). Abu al-Baqa' said: ﴿سُنَّةَ﴾ is in the accusative as an infinitive, meaning: "We have established with you a sunnah like that of those prophets who came before," and it is permissible that it be an object, meaning: "follow the sunnah of those whom We sent," as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ﴾ (Al-An'am: 90). End of quotation. This is a meaning other than the first, and the exegetes follow the first, which is the one that fits the meaning of the verse before it. ﴿ولَنْ تَجِدَ﴾ (and you will not find) for what We have made habitual a ﴿تَحْوِيلًا﴾ (taḥwil, "alteration") from it to something else, since every event has a specific time and a specific attribute. The negation of finding here, and in what is similar to it, means the negation of existence.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on Surah 17, verses 73–77:**

﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We have revealed to you, so that you would fabricate against Us other than it; then they would have taken you as a close friend.﴾ ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would have almost inclined toward them a little.﴾ ﴿Then We would have made you taste a double portion of life and a double portion of death; then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us.﴾ ﴿And indeed they almost tried to drive you out of the land to expel you from it; then they would not have remained after you except a little.﴾ ﴿[This is] the way of those We sent before you of Our messengers, and you will not find any alteration in Our way.﴾

They mentioned various occasions of revelation (asbab al-nuzul), and some of them contain what cannot be correctly attributed to the Messenger ﷺ. This can be consulted in the tafsir of Ibn 'Atiyyah, al-Zamakhshari, al-Tahrir, and others.

The connection (munasabah) of this verse to what precedes it is that when Allah the Exalted enumerated His blessings upon the children of Adam, and then mentioned their condition in the Hereafter, including the giving of the record in the right hand to the people of happiness and the blindness of the people of misery, He followed this with what the wretched in this world intend, namely deceit, trickery and confusion against the master of the people of happiness, who is definitively guaranteed protection (al-ma'sum). The meaning of ﴿لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ﴾ (la-yaftinunaka) is "they would deceive you." This refers to their assumption, not that they had come close to it, since he, peace be upon him, is protected from having them come close to tempting him away from what Allah revealed to him. Their approach to this, in their view, was caused by their hope that he would fabricate against Allah something other than what Allah revealed to him, such as changing a promise into a threat or a threat into a promise, and by what Thaqif proposed, namely that he attribute to Allah what had not been sent down to him. [p. 65]

Then the Qur'an says: ﴿وكَأيِّنْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ هي أشَدُّ قُوَّةً مِن قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتِي أخْرَجَتْكَ﴾ (Muhammad: 13), "And how many a town, stronger than your town which expelled you..." meaning: its people expelled you. In the hadith: "Would that I were a young man when your people expel you." He said: "Will they expel me?" etc. This indicates that they did expel him, but the expulsion that is the cause of the attempt did not occur, so there is no contradiction between the two verses and the hadith. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: He did not go out because of their expulsion, but went out by Allah's command, and thus the contradiction disappears. End of quotation.

﴿ولا يَلْبَثُونَ﴾ (wa-la yalbathuna, "and they would not remain") is the answer of an omitted oath, meaning: "by Allah, if they had driven you out and you went out, they would not remain." For this reason (idhan) did not govern, because it was placed between the estimated oath and the verb, and ﴿فَلا يَلْبَثُونَ﴾ is not directed at it from the standpoint of grammatical case (i'rab). It is possible that ﴿لا يَلْبَثُونَ﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, indicated by the meaning, whose estimation is: "and they, [then] they would not remain," so ﴿وإذًا﴾ fell between the subject and its predicate and was thus disregarded.

Ubayy read ﴿وإذًا لا يَلْبَثُوا﴾ (wa-idhan la yalbathu) with the nun deleted, making idhan operative and putting the verb in the subjunctive, according to the view of the majority; and with an implied "an" (an) after it, according to the view of some. Likewise it is so in the codex of 'Abd Allah, with the nun deleted.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: what is the basis of the two readings? I say: As for the widely known reading, in it the verb is conjoined to the verb while it is in the nominative, because it occurs as the predicate of kada, and the verb in the predicate of kada occupies the position of a noun. As for the reading of Ubayy, in it the whole clause, which is "wa-idhan la yalbathu", is conjoined to the clause of His saying: ﴿وإنْ كادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ﴾. End of quotation. 'Ata' read ﴿لا يُلَبَّثُونَ﴾ (la yulabbathuna) with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the lam and the ba' doubled. Ya'qub read likewise, except that he kasra'd the ba'. The Two Brothers (al-Akhawan), Ibn 'Amir and Hafs read ﴿خِلافَكَ﴾ (khilafaka, "after you / in opposition to you"), and the rest of the seven read ﴿خَلْفَكَ﴾ (khalfaka, "behind you"), and the meaning is one. The poet said:

*The dwellings have been effaced after them, as if the palm-branch-weavers had spread a mat between them.*

This is like His saying: ﴿فَرِحَ المُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلافَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ﴾ (Al-Tawbah: 81), meaning: "behind the Messenger of Allah," according to one of the interpretations. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah read: ﴿بَعْدَكَ﴾ (ba'daka, "after you") in place of ﴿خَلْفَكَ﴾. The better view is that it be taken as an explanation of khalfaka rather than as a reading, because it does not contradict the written text of the codex. He intended to make clear that khalfaka here is not a place-adverb; rather, it is used as a time-adverb with the meaning of ba'daka ("after you"). These adverbs, such as qabl and ba'd and the like, are regularly annexed to concrete nouns, with an omitted modifier indicated by what precedes it, as in khalfaka, meaning "behind your expulsion" (khalfa ikhrajika); and "Zayd came before 'Amr," meaning "before the coming of 'Amr"; and "Bakr laughed after Khalid," meaning "after the laughter of Khalid."

The meaning is that every people who expelled their messenger from among them, Allah's sunnah is that He destroys them after his expulsion and uproots them, and they do not remain after him except a little. Al-Farra' said: ﴿سُنَّةَ﴾ is in the accusative by dropping the preposition, because the meaning is "like the sunnah," so it is put in the accusative after the omission of the kaf; and according to this, one does not stop at His saying: ﴿إلّا قَلِيلًا﴾ (Al-Isra': 85). Abu al-Baqa' said: ﴿سُنَّةَ﴾ is in the accusative as an infinitive, meaning: "We have established with you a sunnah like that of those prophets who came before," and it is permissible that it be an object, meaning: "follow the sunnah of those whom We sent," as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ﴾ (Al-An'am: 90). End of quotation. This is a meaning other than the first, and the exegetes follow the first, which is the one that fits the meaning of the verse before it. ﴿ولَنْ تَجِدَ﴾ (and you will not find) for what We have made habitual a ﴿تَحْوِيلًا﴾ (taḥwil, "alteration") from it to something else, since every event has a specific time and a specific attribute. The negation of finding here, and in what is similar to it, means the negation of existence.

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on Surah 17, verses 73–77:**

﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We have revealed to you, so that you would fabricate against Us other than it; then they would have taken you as a close friend.﴾ ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would have almost inclined toward them a little.﴾ ﴿Then We would have made you taste a double portion of life and a double portion of death; then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us.﴾ ﴿And indeed they almost tried to drive you out of the land to expel you from it; then they would not have remained after you except a little.﴾ ﴿[This is] the way of those We sent before you of Our messengers, and you will not find any alteration in Our way.﴾

Regarding the pronoun in ﴿وإنْ كادُوا﴾ (wa-in kadu, "and indeed they almost"), it has been said that it refers to Quraysh, and it has been said that it refers to Thaqif. They mentioned various occasions of revelation (asbab al-nuzul), and some of them contain what cannot be correctly attributed to the Messenger ﷺ. This can be consulted in the tafsir of Ibn 'Atiyyah, al-Zamakhshari, al-Tahrir, and others.

The connection (munasabah) of this verse to what precedes it is that when Allah the Exalted enumerated His blessings upon the children of Adam, and then mentioned their condition in the Hereafter, including the giving of the record in the right hand to the people of happiness and the blindness of the people of misery, He followed this with what the wretched in this world intend, namely deceit, trickery and confusion against the master of the people of happiness, who is definitively guaranteed protection (al-ma'sum). The meaning of ﴿لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ﴾ (la-yaftinunaka) is "they would deceive you." This refers to their assumption, not that they had come close to it, since he, peace be upon him, is protected from having them come close to tempting him away from what Allah revealed to him. Their approach to this, in their view, was caused by their hope that he would fabricate against Allah something other than what Allah revealed to him, such as changing a promise into a threat or a threat into a promise, and by what Thaqif proposed, namely that he attribute to Allah what had not been sent down to him. [p. 65]

The (إنْ) in this verse is the lightened form (al-mukhaffafah) of the heavy (al-thaqilah) إنَّ. Its governed element is the verbal clause (al-jumlah al-fi'liyyah), which is ﴿كادُوا﴾ (kadu), because it is among the verbs of approximation (af'al al-muqarabah). It enters on the verbs that govern the affirmative particles (al-nawasikh), according to the school of the Basrans, as is established in the science of grammar. The lam in ﴿لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ﴾ (la-yaftinunaka) is the lam that distinguishes this إنْ from the negating إنِ. The word ﴿وإذًا﴾ (wa-idhan, "then") is a particle of response and consequence. An oath is presumed here, and ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ (la-ittakhadhukum, "they would have taken you") is its answer. The estimation is: "by Allah, then [they would have taken you as a friend]", i.e., if you were tempted and fabricated, they would have taken you [as a close friend]. The phrase ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ has the meaning of ﴿لَيَتَّخِذُونَكَ﴾ (la-yattakhidhunaka, "they will take you"), like His saying ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحًا فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا لَظَلُّوا﴾ (Al-Rum: 51), meaning "they will surely remain" (la-yazallunna), because إذًا implies the future, since in meaning it is a conditional, so its place is estimated with a conditional particle.

Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿وإذًا لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ means: "And if you followed their desire, they would have taken you as a close friend, and you would have become their ally, and you would have left My guardianship." End of quotation. This is an explanation of the meaning, and it is not that ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ is the answer of an omitted لو (law). Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿ولَوْلا أنْ ثَبَّتْناكَ﴾ (wa-law la an thabbatnaka) means: "Had it not been for Our making you firm and Our protection, you would have almost inclined toward them," meaning you would have come close to leaning toward their deceit and their trickery. This is an incitement from Allah to him and an act of grace in making him firm, and in it is gentleness toward the believers. ﴿إذَنْ لَوْ قارَبْتَ تَرْكَنُ إلَيْهِمْ أدْنى رَكْنَةٍ﴾ means: if you had come close to inclining toward them even by the least inclination, ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ ضِعْفَ الحَياةِ وضِعْفَ المَماتِ﴾ means: We would have made you taste the punishment of the Hereafter and the punishment of the grave, doubled. If you ask: what is the real structure of this speech? I say: its origin is ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ punishment of life and punishment of death, because punishment is of two kinds: punishment at death, which is the punishment of the grave, and punishment in the life of the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the Fire. The word "double" (ḍi'f) can be described by it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَآتِهِمْ عَذابًا ضِعْفًا مِنَ النّارِ﴾ (Al-A'raf: 38), meaning "doubled." So the original speech was ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ a double punishment in life and a double punishment at death. Then the described noun was omitted and the attribute was put in its place, which is "double", and then the attribute was made an annexed noun in the manner of the described noun, so it was said ﴿ضِعْفَ الحَياةِ وضِعْفَ المَماتِ﴾, just as it is said ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ "painful life and painful death." It is also permissible that "double of life" means the punishment of the worldly life, and "double of death" means what follows death of the punishment of the grave and the punishment of the Fire. The meaning is: We would have doubled for you the punishment hastened for the disobedient in worldly life, and what We delay for after death. End of quotation.

The answer to (لَوْلا) (law la), when it is affirmative, requires its negation because of the existence of what precedes it. So the approach to inclining did not occur from him, let alone the inclining itself, and what prevented that is the existence of Allah's making him firm. Qatadah, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibn Musarrif read ﴿تَرْكُنُ﴾ (tarkunu) with a damma on the kaf, as the present tense of ركَنَ (raka-na) with a fatha on it. The word ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ (shay'an) is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar) [of degree]. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: he means the doubled punishment of life and the doubled punishment of death, in the sense that what the one who sins deserves of Our punishment in this world and the Hereafter, We would have doubled. Ibn al-Anbari held that the meaning is: they almost reported about you that you had inclined to their speech because of their action toward it, figuratively and by extension, as you say to a man: "You almost killed yourself", meaning: "the people almost killed you because of what you did."

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger ﷺ was protected, but this is an instruction for the community, lest anyone among them incline toward the polytheists in any matter of Allah's rulings and laws. End of quotation. The lam in ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ (la-adhaqnaka) is the answer of an omitted oath before (إذًا) (idhan), meaning: "by Allah, if inclining occurs, then it would certainly be such." The discussion of ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ is like the discussion of ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ regarding the past tense being placed in the position of the present tense that is preceded by the lam and the nun. Among those who explicitly stated that the lam in ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ and ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ is the lam of the oath is al-Hawfi. Al-Zamakhshari said: In the mention of the great wrong and its causation, together with following it with a severe threat of doubled punishment in both abodes, is clear evidence that a wrong's ugliness is magnified in proportion to the greatness of the status of its doer and the elevation of his rank. End of quotation. Among this is His saying: ﴿يا نِساءَ النَّبِيِّ مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ﴾ (Al-Ahzab: 30), "O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality..." etc. Al-Zamakhshari said: In it there is a slight flattery toward the deluded, opposition to Allah, and departure from His guardianship, and a cause that requires His anger and His punishment. End of quotation.

It has been narrated that when this was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye." (p. 66) Al-Hadrami said: The pronoun in ﴿وإنْ كادُوا﴾ refers to the Jews of Medina and its surroundings, such as Huyayy ibn Akhtab and others, because they went to plot against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "This land is not the land of the prophets; the land of the prophets is al-Sham. But you fear the Romans. So if you are a prophet, go out to it, for Allah will protect you as He protected other prophets." So this verse was revealed, and Allah the Exalted informed that if he had gone out, He would not have left them after that ﴿إلّا قَلِيلًا﴾ (illa qalilan, "except a little").

Al-Naqqash related that he went out because of their words, and encamped at Dhu al-Hulayfah, and remained waiting for his companions, and then this verse was revealed and he returned. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This is weak; it did not occur in any biography or any book that is relied upon, and Dhu al-Hulayfah is not on the route from Medina to al-Sham. End of quotation.

A group said: The pronoun refers to Quraysh, as said by Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah. Their attempt to expel him (istifzazuhum) is what they undertook of expelling him from Mecca, as they undertook to confine him in the valley (al-Shi'b). Their attempt at expulsion occurred after the revelation of the verse, and they constrained him until he went out, and they followed him to the cave, and the threat was carried out against them in that they did not remain ﴿إلّا قَلِيلًا﴾ on the day of Badr. Al-Zajjaj, reporting that their attempt to expel him was what they agreed upon in the Dar al-Nadwah (the assembly house of Quraysh) of killing him, and the "land" in this view is the world. Mujahid said: Quraysh went in that direction, but it did not happen from them, because when Allah the Exalted wanted to preserve Quraysh and not to uproot them, He permitted His Messenger to emigrate, so he went out by His permission, not by the compulsion of Quraysh, and Quraysh was preserved so that from them and their descendants those who would accept Islam might become Muslims. He said: Had Quraysh expelled him, they would have been punished. Mujahid held that the pronoun in ﴿يَلْبَثُونَ﴾ (yalbathuna) refers to all of them.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ﴾ (la-yastafizzunaka) means "they would tempt you away from your opinion." Ibn 'Isa said: "they would unsettle you and make you light." And he recited:

*He obeys the fool of the people when he provokes him, and disobeys the forbearing one whom the calamities have whitened.*

An oath is presumed here, and ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ (la-ittakhadhukum, "they would have taken you") is its answer. The estimation is: "by Allah, then [they would have taken you as a friend]", i.e., if you were tempted and fabricated, they would have taken you [as a close friend]. The phrase ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ has the meaning of ﴿لَيَتَّخِذُونَكَ﴾ (la-yattakhidhunaka, "they will take you"), like His saying ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحًا فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا لَظَلُّوا﴾ (Al-Rum: 51), meaning "they will surely remain" (la-yazallunna), because إذًا implies the future, since in meaning it is a conditional, so its place is estimated with a conditional particle.

Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿وإذًا لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ means: "And if you followed their desire, they would have taken you as a close friend, and you would have become their ally, and you would have left My guardianship." End of quotation. This is an explanation of the meaning, and it is not that ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ is the answer of an omitted لو (law). Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿ولَوْلا أنْ ثَبَّتْناكَ﴾ (wa-law la an thabbatnaka) means: "Had it not been for Our making you firm and Our protection, you would have almost inclined toward them," meaning you would have come close to leaning toward their deceit and their trickery. This is an incitement from Allah to him and an act of grace in making him firm, and in it is gentleness toward the believers. ﴿إذَنْ لَوْ قارَبْتَ تَرْكَنُ إلَيْهِمْ أدْنى رَكْنَةٍ﴾ means: if you had come close to inclining toward them even by the least inclination, ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ ضِعْفَ الحَياةِ وضِعْفَ المَماتِ﴾ means: We would have made you taste the punishment of the Hereafter and the punishment of the grave, doubled. If you ask: what is the real structure of this speech? I say: its origin is ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ punishment of life and punishment of death, because punishment is of two kinds: punishment at death, which is the punishment of the grave, and punishment in the life of the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the Fire. The word "double" (ḍi'f) can be described by it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَآتِهِمْ عَذابًا ضِعْفًا مِنَ النّارِ﴾ (Al-A'raf: 38), meaning "doubled." So the original speech was ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ a double punishment in life and a double punishment at death. Then the described noun was omitted and the attribute was put in its place, which is "double", and then the attribute was made an annexed noun in the manner of the described noun, so it was said ﴿ضِعْفَ الحَياةِ وضِعْفَ المَماتِ﴾, just as it is said ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ "painful life and painful death." It is also permissible that "double of life" means the punishment of the worldly life, and "double of death" means what follows death of the punishment of the grave and the punishment of the Fire. The meaning is: We would have doubled for you the punishment hastened for the disobedient in worldly life, and what We delay for after death. End of quotation.

The answer to (لَوْلا) (law la), when it is affirmative, requires its negation because of the existence of what precedes it. So the approach to inclining did not occur from him, let alone the inclining itself, and what prevented that is the existence of Allah's making him firm. Qatadah, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibn Musarrif read ﴿تَرْكُنُ﴾ (tarkunu) with a damma on the kaf, as the present tense of ركَنَ (raka-na) with a fatha on it. The word ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ (shay'an) is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar) [of degree]. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: he means the doubled punishment of life and the doubled punishment of death, in the sense that what the one who sins deserves of Our punishment in this world and the Hereafter, We would have doubled. Ibn al-Anbari held that the meaning is: they almost reported about you that you had inclined to their speech because of their action toward it, figuratively and by extension, as you say to a man: "You almost killed yourself", meaning: "the people almost killed you because of what you did."

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger ﷺ was protected, but this is an instruction for the community, lest anyone among them incline toward the polytheists in any matter of Allah's rulings and laws. End of quotation. The lam in ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ (la-adhaqnaka) is the answer of an omitted oath before (إذًا) (idhan), meaning: "by Allah, if inclining occurs, then it would certainly be such." The discussion of ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ is like the discussion of ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ regarding the past tense being placed in the position of the present tense that is preceded by the lam and the nun. Among those who explicitly stated that the lam in ﴿لاتَّخَذُوكَ﴾ and ﴿لَأذَقْناكَ﴾ is the lam of the oath is al-Hawfi. Al-Zamakhshari said: In the mention of the great wrong and its causation, together with following it with a severe threat of doubled punishment in both abodes, is clear evidence that a wrong's ugliness is magnified in proportion to the greatness of the status of its doer and the elevation of his rank. End of quotation. Among this is His saying: ﴿يا نِساءَ النَّبِيِّ مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ﴾ (Al-Ahzab: 30), "O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality..." etc. Al-Zamakhshari said: In it there is a slight flattery toward the deluded, opposition to Allah, and departure from His guardianship, and a cause that requires His anger and His punishment. End of quotation.

It has been narrated that when this was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye." (p. 66) Al-Hadrami said: The pronoun in ﴿وإنْ كادُوا﴾ refers to the Jews of Medina and its surroundings, such as Huyayy ibn Akhtab and others, because they went to plot against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "This land is not the land of the prophets; the land of the prophets is al-Sham. But you fear the Romans. So if you are a prophet, go out to it, for Allah will protect you as He protected other prophets." So this verse was revealed, and Allah the Exalted informed that if he had gone out, He would not have left them after that ﴿إلّا قَلِيلًا﴾ (illa qalilan, "except a little").

Al-Naqqash related that he went out because of their words, and encamped at Dhu al-Hulayfah, and remained waiting for his companions, and then this verse was revealed and he returned. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This is weak; it did not occur in any biography or any book that is relied upon, and Dhu al-Hulayfah is not on the route from Medina to al-Sham. End of quotation.

A group said: The pronoun refers to Quraysh, as said by Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah. Their attempt to expel him (istifzazuhum) is what they undertook of expelling him from Mecca, as they undertook to confine him in the valley (al-Shi'b). Their attempt at expulsion occurred after the revelation of the verse, and they constrained him until he went out, and they followed him to the cave, and the threat was carried out against them in that they did not remain ﴿إلّا قَلِيلًا﴾ on the day of Badr. Al-Zajjaj, reporting that their attempt to expel him was what they agreed upon in the Dar al-Nadwah (the assembly house of Quraysh) of killing him, and the "land" in this view is the world. Mujahid said: Quraysh went in that direction, but it did not happen from them, because when Allah the Exalted wanted to preserve Quraysh and not to uproot them, He permitted His Messenger to emigrate, so he went out by His permission, not by the compulsion of Quraysh, and Quraysh was preserved so that from them and their descendants those who would accept Islam might become Muslims. He said: Had Quraysh expelled him, they would have been punished. Mujahid held that the pronoun in ﴿يَلْبَثُونَ﴾ (yalbathuna) refers to all of them.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ﴾ (la-yastafizzunaka) means "they would tempt you away from your opinion." Ibn 'Isa said: "they would unsettle you and make you light." And he recited:

*He obeys the fool of the people when he provokes him, and disobeys the forbearing one whom the calamities have whitened.*

The apparent meaning is that the verse indicates the approach of their attempt to drive him out, so the attempt did not occur, nor did their actual expulsion of him, which was the cause of the attempt. Then the Qur'an says: ﴿وكَأيِّنْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ هي أشَدُّ قُوَّةً مِن قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتِي أخْرَجَتْكَ﴾ (Muhammad: 13), "And how many a town, stronger than your town which expelled you..." meaning: its people expelled you. In the hadith: "Would that I were a young man when your people expel you." He said: "Will they expel me?" etc. This indicates that they did expel him, but the expulsion that is the cause of the attempt did not occur, so there is no contradiction between the two verses and the hadith. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: He did not go out because of their expulsion, but went out by Allah's command, and thus the contradiction disappears. End of quotation.

﴿ولا يَلْبَثُونَ﴾ (wa-la yalbathuna, "and they would not remain") is the answer of an omitted oath, meaning: "by Allah, if they had driven you out and you went out, they would not remain." For this reason (idhan) did not govern, because it was placed between the estimated oath and the verb, and ﴿فَلا يَلْبَثُونَ﴾ is not directed at it from the standpoint of grammatical case (i'rab). It is possible that ﴿لا يَلْبَثُونَ﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, indicated by the meaning, whose estimation is: "and they, [then] they would not remain," so ﴿وإذًا﴾ fell between the subject and its predicate and was thus disregarded.

Ubayy read ﴿وإذًا لا يَلْبَثُوا﴾ (wa-idhan la yalbathu) with the nun deleted, making idhan operative and putting the verb in the subjunctive, according to the view of the majority; and with an implied "an" (an) after it, according to the view of some. Likewise it is so in the codex of 'Abd Allah, with the nun deleted.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: what is the basis of the two readings? I say: As for the widely known reading, in it the verb is conjoined to the verb while it is in the nominative, because it occurs as the predicate of kada, and the verb in the predicate of kada occupies the position of a noun. As for the reading of Ubayy, in it the whole clause, which is "wa-idhan la yalbathu", is conjoined to the clause of His saying: ﴿وإنْ كادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ﴾. End of quotation. 'Ata' read ﴿لا يُلَبَّثُونَ﴾ (la yulabbathuna) with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the lam and the ba' doubled. Ya'qub read likewise, except that he kasra'd the ba'. The Two Brothers (al-Akhawan), Ibn 'Amir and Hafs read ﴿خِلافَكَ﴾ (khilafaka, "after you / in opposition to you"), and the rest of the seven read ﴿خَلْفَكَ﴾ (khalfaka, "behind you"), and the meaning is one. The poet said:

*The dwellings have been effaced after them, as if the palm-branch-weavers had spread a mat between them.*

This is like His saying: ﴿فَرِحَ المُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلافَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ﴾ (Al-Tawbah: 81), meaning: "behind the Messenger of Allah," according to one of the interpretations. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah read: ﴿بَعْدَكَ﴾ (ba'daka, "after you") in place of ﴿خَلْفَكَ﴾. The better view is that it be taken as an explanation of khalfaka rather than as a reading, because it does not contradict the written text of the codex. He intended to make clear that khalfaka here is not a place-adverb; rather, it is used as a time-adverb with the meaning of ba'daka ("after you"). These adverbs, such as qabl and ba'd and the like, are regularly annexed to concrete nouns, with an omitted modifier indicated by what precedes it, as in khalfaka, meaning "behind your expulsion" (khalfa ikhrajika); and "Zayd came before 'Amr," meaning "before the coming of 'Amr"; and "Bakr laughed after Khalid," meaning "after the laughter of Khalid."

﴿سُنَّةَ﴾ (sunnata) is in the accusative as an emphatic infinitive, meaning: Allah established a sunnah (established way). The meaning is that every people who expelled their messenger from among them, Allah's sunnah is that He destroys them after his expulsion and uproots them, and they do not remain after him except a little. Al-Farra' said: ﴿سُنَّةَ﴾ is in the accusative by dropping the preposition, because the meaning is "like the sunnah," so it is put in the accusative after the omission of the kaf; and according to this, one does not stop at His saying: ﴿إلّا قَلِيلًا﴾ (Al-Isra': 85). Abu al-Baqa' said: ﴿سُنَّةَ﴾ is in the accusative as an infinitive, meaning: "We have established with you a sunnah like that of those prophets who came before," and it is permissible that it be an object, meaning: "follow the sunnah of those whom We sent," as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ﴾ (Al-An'am: 90). End of quotation. This is a meaning other than the first, and the exegetes follow the first, which is the one that fits the meaning of the verse before it. ﴿ولَنْ تَجِدَ﴾ (and you will not find) for what We have made habitual a ﴿تَحْوِيلًا﴾ (taḥwil, "alteration") from it to something else, since every event has a specific time and a specific attribute. The negation of finding here, and in what is similar to it, means the negation of existence.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 17, verse 78–86 (part 1 of 3):

﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.﴾ ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud (voluntary night prayer) with it as an additional devotion for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.﴾ ﴿And say: "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself an authority to help me."﴾ ﴿And say: "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish."﴾ ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾ ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself, and when evil touches him, he is ever despairing.﴾ ﴿Say: "Each acts according to his manner, but your Lord knows best who is best guided in way."﴾ ﴿And they ask you about the soul. Say: "The soul is of the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little."﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you; then you would not find for yourself against Us any advocate,﴾ ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His favor upon you has ever been great.﴾ [al-Isra': 87] ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants."﴾ [al-Isra': 88] ﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every example, but most of the people refused except disbelief.﴾ [al-Isra': 89] ﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause to gush forth for us a spring from the earth,﴾ [al-Isra': 90] ﴿or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes and make rivers gush forth within it in abundance,﴾ [al-Isra': 91] ﴿or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments as you claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee,﴾ [al-Isra': 92] ﴿or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I but a human messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 93] ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 94] ﴿Say: "If there were in the earth angels walking calmly, We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger."﴾ [al-Isra': 95] ﴿Say: "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever Acquainted with and Seeing of His servants."﴾ [al-Isra': 96] ﴿And whomever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, and whomever He sends astray, you will not find for them protectors apart from Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind and mute and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; whenever its fire subsides, We increase for them its blaze.﴾ [al-Isra': 97] ﴿That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, "When we are bones and crumbled remains, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ [al-Isra': 98] ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is Able to create their likes? And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, but the wrongdoers refused except disbelief.﴾ [al-Isra': 99] ﴿Say: "If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold them for fear of expenditure. And man has ever been tight-fisted."﴾ [al-Isra': 100] ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched."﴾ [al-Isra': 101] ﴿He said, "You have certainly known that these have not sent down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence, and indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed."﴾ [al-Isra': 102] ﴿So he intended to expel them from the land, but We drowned him and whoever was with him, all together.﴾ [al-Isra': 103] ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, "Dwell in the land; and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed multitude."﴾ [al-Isra': 104] ﴿And with truth We sent it down, and with truth it descended, and We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.﴾ [al-Isra': 105] ﴿And a Qur'an which We have separated that you may recite it to the people over a duration, and We have sent it down in stages.﴾ [al-Isra': 106] ﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration,﴾ [al-Isra': 107] ﴿and say, "Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has ever been fulfilled."﴾ [al-Isra': 108] ﴿And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.﴾ [al-Isra': 109] ﴿Say: "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call, to Him belong the most beautiful names." And do not recite your prayer aloud or quietly, but seek between that a middle way.﴾ [al-Isra': 110] ﴿And say: "Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and has no protector out of weakness," and glorify Him with great glorification.﴾ [al-Isra': 111]

(The commentary on the words of Allah, "Establish prayer...") The connection of ﴿Establish prayer﴾ with what precedes it is that when He mentioned their plotting against the Messenger and what they intended by it, He commanded him to turn to his own affair of worshipping his Lord and not to occupy his heart with them. The discussion had already preceded concerning theology, the return (resurrection), and prophethood, so He followed that with the command to the most noble of acts of worship and obedience after faith, which is prayer. The discussion of establishing prayer has already occurred, and the address of the command was directed to the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace. The lam in ﴿li-dulūki﴾ — they said it means "after," i.e., after the decline (dulūk) of the sun, as they said this regarding the people of Mutammim ibn Nuwayra, lamenting his brother Malik:

"When we separated, it was as though I and Malik, after a long gathering, had not spent a single night together."

I.e., after a long gathering. And from this (usage) is his writing "on the third of such and such month" (lithalāth khalawna min shahr kadhā). Al-Wahidi said: the lam is for causation, because prayer becomes obligatory only with the decline of the sun, so it is obligatory upon the one praying to establish it because of the decline of the sun. Ibn Atiyya said: ﴿Establish prayer﴾ and the rest of the verse — this, by consensus of the exegetes, refers to the obligatory prayers. Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Burda, al-Hasan and the majority said: the decline of the sun is its passing the zenith, and the reference is to Dhuhr and 'Asr; and the darkness of the night refers to Maghrib and 'Isha'. ﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾ is intended to mean the Subh prayer, so the verse according to this encompasses all the prayers.

Ibn Mas'ud narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me at the decline of the sun when it passed the zenith, and he led me in the Dhuhr prayer." Jabir narrated that the Prophet ﷺ went out from his place after eating, and the sun had passed its zenith, and he said: "Go out, O Abu Bakr, for this is the time when the sun has declined." Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam said: the decline of the sun is its setting, and the reference by it is to Maghrib; (and the darkness of the night) is its gloom, so the reference is to 'Atama (the night prayer). ﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾ is the Subh prayer, and no reference according to this interpretation is made to Dhuhr and 'Asr. End. And from Ali it is reported that it is the setting. The lam and ilā are connected to aqim, so ilā is a limit for establishing (the prayer). Abu al-Baqa' permitted that it be a circumstantial accusative (hal) of the prayer, saying: meaning "extended." By "the recitation of dawn" he means the Subh prayer, and it was singled out with the word "Qur'an," which is recitation, because its recitation is great, since its recitation is long and loudly voiced. ﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾ is in the accusative as a conjunction to (al-salāh, "the prayer").

Al-Akhfash said: it is in the accusative by an implied verb, its estimate being "and devote yourself to the recitation of dawn" or "upon you is the recitation of dawn." End. The Subh prayer was named after some of what occurs in it. Al-Zamakhshari said: the Fajr prayer was named "Qur'an," which is recitation, because it is a pillar, just as it was named ruku' (bowing), sujud (prostration) and qunut (devout standing), and it is a proof against Ibn Abi Ulayya and al-Asamm in their claim that recitation is not a pillar. End. It was said: if we interpret dulūk as the decline of the sun, the time becomes shared between Dhuhr and 'Asr, when the establishment is limited by the darkness of the night, and the darkness (ghasaq) becomes a time shared between Maghrib and 'Isha'; and the mentioned would be three times: the beginning of the time of decline, the beginning of the time of Maghrib, and the beginning of the time of Fajr. End. What the apparent wording indicates is that it is a command to establish prayer either from the beginning of the decline until the darkness, and with the recitation of dawn; or from the setting until the darkness and with the recitation of dawn. Thus the thing commanded is prayer at two times, and the times of the five prayers are not derived from this wording in any way.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said, regarding His words ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn﴾, that it is evidence that the prayer is not complete except with recitation, because the command is for obligation, and recitation at that time is obligatory only within prayer. Whoever says that the meaning of ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn﴾ is the dawn prayer has erred, because he has turned the speech from its literal meaning to the figurative without evidence. Also, in the sequence of the recitation comes ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it as a supererogatory prayer for you﴾, and it is impossible to perform tahajjud with the dawn prayer at night. The pronoun in (bihi, "with it") refers to ﴿the Qur'an of dawn﴾ mentioned before it, so it is established that the intended meaning is the very Qur'an, not the place of tahajjud with the recited Qur'an in the dawn prayer, nor the impossibility of tahajjud at night with the dawn prayer. And even if it were possible for the intended meaning to be what they mentioned, its evidence would still stand for the obligation of recitation in prayer, because recitation was never used as an expression for prayer except that it is one of its pillars. End. There is some abridgement in it.

The apparent meaning is that it is recommended (nadb) to perform the dawn prayer at the beginning of its time, because He commanded the performance of ﴿the Qur'an of dawn﴾, so it would require obligation at the first emergence of dawn. But consensus (ijma') prevented that, so the recommendation remained, due to the existence of the requirement, and when its obligation is removed, its recommendation remains. He repeated ﴿the Qur'an of dawn﴾ in His words ﴿Indeed, the Qur'an of dawn﴾ and did not use a pronoun, which indicates the honouring and highlighting of the Qur'an of dawn. The meaning of ﴿mashhudan﴾ ("witnessed") is that it is witnessed by the angels, the guardians of the night and the guardians of the day, as came in the hadith: "They succeed one another, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer." This is the view of the majority. It has been said: it is witnessed by many of the worshippers customarily. It has also been said: it is required that a large congregation witness it. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn﴾ is an exhortation to lengthen the recitation in the dawn prayer, since it is a prayer in which people are gathered so that they hear the Qur'an and the reward increases; for this reason the dawn prayer was the longest of the prayers in recitation. End. By his words "an exhortation" he means that the implied sense is: "and upon you [is] the Qur'an of dawn," or "and keep to it."

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn 'Askar said: ﴿mashhudan﴾ means that Allah and His angels witness it, and he mentioned the hadith of Abu al-Darda', that He descends in the last part of the night. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi has a discussion regarding His words ﴿mashhudan﴾ according to his habit in interpreting the Book of Allah in ways the Arabs would not understand. What should be followed, indeed what must not be deviated from, is what the Messenger (ﷺ) explained it with, when he said regarding it: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it." At-Tirmidhi said of it: a hadith, hasan sahih.

When Allah commanded him to establish the prayer at the stated time, and His command did not indicate that it was specific to him to the exclusion of his community, He mentioned what He singled him out for and made obligatory upon him from qiyam al-layl, which for his community is voluntary. So He said: ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it﴾, i.e., with the Qur'an in prayer, ﴿as a supererogatory prayer (nafilah) for you﴾, specifically for you. Here tahajjud is of the form tafa''ala in the sense of removal and abandonment, like their saying: ta'atthama and tahannatha meaning "he abandoned sin" and "he abandoned the taḥannuth," and from it: "I tahannathtu in the cave of Hira'," i.e., I abandoned the taḥannuth; and it is explained by its implication, which is worship (al-ta'abbud). ("From") here is for partitive meaning (lil-tab'id).

Al-Hawfi said: "from" is connected to a verb indicated by the meaning of the speech, its estimate being: "and stay awake from the night with the Qur'an." He said: It is possible that the estimate be: "and rise after a sleep from the night." Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "from" is partitive; the estimate is "a time of the night," i.e., "and rise a time of the night." Al-Zamakhshari said: "and from the night" means "and upon you [is] part of the night, ﴿so perform tahajjud with it﴾," and tahajjud is abandoning sleep for prayer. End. If his explanation "and upon you [is] part of the night" is an explanation of meaning, it is close; but if he intended grammatical and i'rab terminology, it is not correct, because the object of an exhortation cannot be a particle, and estimating "min" as "bi-ba'd" (with part) is an imprecision, because it is not at all synonymous with it; for had it been synonymous with it, it would necessarily be a noun, and no one holds that. Do you not see the consensus of the grammarians that waw in "ma'a" is a particle even though it is estimated as "ma'a"? The apparent view is that the pronoun in "bihi" refers to the Qur'an, since it was mentioned before, and the idafah (genitive construction) is not considered in it; the estimate is ﴿fa-tahajjad﴾ "with the Qur'an" in prayer. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: the pronoun in "bihi" refers to the time estimated in "wa-qum waqtan min al-layl." End. Then the bi is adverbial of time, i.e., "perform tahajjud in it." "Nafilah" is in the accusative. Al-Hawfi said: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun, i.e., "We have given you a supererogatory gift (nafilah)." He said: "nafilah" may also be accusative by "tahajjad" if you take it to the meaning "pray with it a supererogatory prayer for you," i.e., "pray a supererogatory prayer for you."

Abu al-Baqa' said: In it there are two views. The first: it is a verbal noun in the sense of tahajjad, i.e., "perform a voluntary act, a voluntary act," and "nafilah" here is a verbal noun like "al-'aqibah." The second: it is a circumstantial accusative (hal), i.e., "a prayer of supererogation." End. It is a hal from the pronoun in "bihi," and it refers to the Qur'an, not to the time that Ibn 'Atiyyah estimated.

Al-Aswad, 'Alqamah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad and al-Hajjaj ibn 'Amr said: tahajjud is after a sleep. Al-Hasan said: it is whatever is after the late night prayer ('isha'). Ibn 'Abbas said: "nafilah" means an increase for you over the obligatory, and qiyam al-layl was obligatory upon him. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: It may be that it is by way of recommendation in voluntary prayer, and the address is to him while the meaning is him and his community, like his address in ﴿Establish the prayer﴾. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: it is only a supererogatory prayer for him, since what preceded and what followed of his sin was forgiven him, on the year of al-Hudaybiyyah; so his supererogatory acts and his seeking forgiveness were virtuous deeds and closer acts of worship, more noble than the supererogatory acts of his community; because these, I mean the supererogatory acts of his community, either make up for their obligatory acts or erase their errors. Al-Tabari weakened the view of Mujahid and al-Dhahabi approved it, Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi also found it good. Muqatil said: "fa-lahuwa" is an honour and a gift for you. It has been said: it was obligatory and then the leave to abandon it was granted. From the hadith of Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani: he observed his prayer (ﷺ) one night, and he prayed thirteen rak'ahs with the witr. From 'A'ishah: he did not increase in Ramadan or other than it beyond eleven rak'ahs.

The meaning of "'asa" with beloved things is hope (tarajji). It has been said: it is on its own basis of hope, its estimate being: "so let it be with hope that ﴿He will raise you﴾." It has been said: it has the meaning of kay (so that). This should be an explanation of meaning. The better view is that this "an" is hope, and the expectation carries the meaning of obligation from Allah, Exalted, and it is connected in meaning to His words ﴿fa-tahajjad﴾. ﴿'Asa﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216] here is complete, and its subject is ﴿an yab'athaka﴾, and "rabbuka" is the agent of "yab'athaka," and "maqaman" apparently is its object, a verbal noun not from the verb's own form, because "yab'athaka" means "yuqimuka" (will make you stand); you say: "uqima min qabrihi" and "bu'itha min qabrihi." Ibn 'Atiyyah said: it is accusative as an adverb of place, i.e., in a praiseworthy station. It has been said: it is accusative as a circumstantial (hal), i.e., possessing a station. It has been said: it is a verbal noun for a deleted verb, the estimate being "fa-taqumu maqaman." It is not permissible for "'asa" here to be a defective verb with the predicate preceding the subject, so that "rabbuka" would be nominative as the subject of "'asa" and "an yab'athaka" the predicate in accusative position with it; except in this last grammatical analysis. But before it, it is not permissible, because "maqaman" is in the accusative governed by "yab'athaka," and "rabbuka" is nominative governed by "'asa," so it would entail separating what is a relative complement from its own complement by a foreign element, and that is not permissible.

Regarding the interpretation of the praiseworthy station, there are several views:

First: that it concerns the matter of the intercession which the prophets push off until it reaches him (ﷺ). The hadith is in the Sahih, and it is a promise from Allah, Exalted, to him, upon him be prayers and peace. In this intercession all the people of the gathering praise him, and in his well-known supplication: "and raise him to the praiseworthy station that You promised him." They agreed that what is meant by it is the intercession.

Second: that it concerns his intercession for his community in bringing out their sinners from the Fire. This intercession occurs only after the reckoning and the entry into Paradise and the entry into the Fire, and in this the prophets do not push it off; rather they intercede, and the scholars intercede. The hadith of this intercession has been narrated, and at its end: "until none remains in the Fire except him whom the Qur'an has detained," i.e., who has become obligated to eternal abiding. He said: then he recited this verse, ﴿It may be that your Lord raises you to a praiseworthy station﴾. From Abu Hurayrah that he (peace be upon him) said: "The praiseworthy station is the station in which I intercede for my community." The apparent meaning of this statement is the restriction of his intercession to his community. Whoever interpreted it as the great intercession, by which all creation praises him, has explained that what is meant is his community and others, or it is said: each of these two stations is praiseworthy.

Third: from Hudhayfah: Allah gathers people on a plain, and no soul speaks; the first one called is Muhammad (ﷺ), and he says: "Labbayka and Sa'daykа, and the evil is not from You. The guided one is he whom You guide, Your servant is before You, by You and to You; there is no refuge nor place of safety except with You. You are blessed and exalted, glory be to You, Lord of the House." He said: this is His words ﴿It may be that your Lord raises you to a praiseworthy station﴾.

Fourth: al-Zamakhshari said: the meaning of the praiseworthy station is the station in which the one standing in it is praised, and everyone who sees it and knows it praises him; and it is general in every thing that brings praise of kinds of honours. End. This is a good view, and for this reason "maqaman mahmudan" is indefinite, so it does not refer to a specific station but every praiseworthy station to which the wording applies.

Fifth: what a group said, including Mujahid, and it was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the praiseworthy station is that Allah seats him with Him upon the Throne. Al-Tabari mentioned a hadith on this, and al-Naqqash narrated from Abu Dawud al-Sijistani that he said: "Whoever denies this hadith is in our view accused; the people of knowledge have always narrated this." Ibn 'Atiyyah said: he means whoever denies its permissibility under its interpretation. Abu 'Amr and Mujahid said: if any of the imams interprets the Qur'an, then he has two views abandoned among the people of knowledge; one of them is this, and the second is in the interpretation of ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 23], he said: it means awaiting the reward, not seeing. The phrase "ma'ahu" may be interpreted as an elevation of its rank and honour over His creation, like His words ﴿Indeed those who are with your Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 206], and His words ﴿Build for me with You a house﴾ [al-Tahrim: 11], and ﴿Indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69]; all of these are an expression of standing, not of place.

Al-Wahidi said: this view is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is a vile, repulsive, appalling view; the like of it cannot be authentically from Ibn 'Abbas. The text of the Book cries out against its corruption from several aspects:

First: that "ba'th" is the opposite of "ijlas" (seating): "ba'athtu al-tarik" (I sent off the one who abandons) and "ba'atha Allah al-mayyit" (Allah raised the dead), meaning He caused him to rise from his grave. So interpreting "ba'th" as "ijlas" is interpreting an opposite by its opposite.

Second: if He were seated, Exalted, upon the Throne, He would be bounded and finite, and would thus be created.

Third: He said "maqaman," and did not say "maq'adan," and "maqam" is the place of standing, not the place of sitting.

Fourth: that the foolish and ignorant say that all the people of Paradise sit with Him, Exalted, and He asks them about their worldly circumstances, so there is no distinction for him through his being seated with Him.

Fifth: that if it is said "the sultan sent so-and-so," it is not understood from it that he seated him with himself. End. There is some abridgement in it.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 17, verse 78–86 (part 3 of 3):

When the Exalted One commanded him to establish the prayer and the tahajjud (night prayer), and promised him that He would raise him to "a praiseworthy station" (maqaman mahmudan), which is in the Hereafter, He commanded him to supplicate with words that encompass his worldly and otherworldly affairs, saying: ﴿And say: "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit."﴾ The apparent meaning is that it is general in all its occasions of entering and exiting, worldly and otherworldly. Here, "sidq" (sound, truthful) is a term that requires the removal of blame and the comprehensiveness of praise, just as you say "rajul sidq" (a man of truth), as it is the opposite of "rajul su'" (a man of evil).

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it is a specific entrance, which is into Madinah, and a specific exit, which is from Makkah. Thus what is mentioned first is what occurs last, and the place of the conjunction "wa" (and) is the more important, so it was begun with. Mujahid and Abu Salih said: its meaning is his entering into what he was burdened with of the responsibilities of prophethood and the conveying of the Shari'ah, and his exiting from it having fulfilled what he was charged with, without negligence. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Cause me to enter the grave" (adkhilni al-qabra) ﴿a sound entrance﴾, an entrance that is pleasing, in a state of purity and goodness from misdeeds; and "cause me to exit from it at the resurrection" an exit that is pleasing, met with honour, safe from wrath; this is indicated by his mention of it alongside the mention of resurrection. It was also said: his entering Makkah victorious over it by conquest, and his exiting from it safe from the polytheists. Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: his entering the cave and his exiting from it safe. It was also said: the exit from Madinah and the entrance to Makkah by conquest. It was said: the entrance into the prayer and the exit from it. It was said: the entrance into Paradise and the exit from Makkah. It was said: the entrance into what he was commanded and the exit from what he was forbidden. It was said: ﴿cause me to enter﴾ into the seas of the proofs of Divine unity and transcendence, ﴿and cause me to exit﴾ from occupation with the proof to knowledge of what is proven, and contemplation of the traces of His created things, to total absorption in knowledge of the One, the Unique. Abu Sahl said: when he returned from Tabuk, after the hypocrites had said: ﴿The mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8], he meant the entrance of might and the exit of victory into Makkah. The best of these sayings is that they be taken as examples rather than specifications, and the wording, as we have mentioned, encompasses all occasions of entering and exiting.

The reading of the majority is ﴿mudkhala﴾ and (mukhraja) with a dammah on their mim, and this is a regular verbal noun (masdar) on the pattern of af'ala, as in "akramtuhu makraman," meaning "ikraman" (I honoured him with honour). Qatadah, Abu Haywah, Humayd and Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah read them with a fathah on both. The author of al-Lawami' said: they are both verbal nouns from "dakhala" and "kharaja," but they come from the meaning of the preceding ﴿adkhilni﴾ and ﴿akhrijni﴾ rather than their wording, and like them is ﴿and He made you grow from the earth a growth﴾ [Nuh: 17]. It is also permissible that both be nouns of place, and their accusative is as adverbs of place. Others said: they are both in the accusative as verbal nouns, under an implied verb, i.e., "cause me to enter, so I enter a sound entrance, and cause me to exit, so I exit a sound exit."

As for "sultan" (authority) here: al-Hasan said: the empowerment over the disbelievers by the sword, and over the hypocrites by establishing the hudud (prescribed punishments). Qatadah said: a mighty kingdom by which You help me against everyone who opposes me. Mujahid said: a clear proof. It was said: a Book containing the hudud and rulings. It was said: the conquest of Makkah. It was said: in every age, a sultan that supports your religion; and "nasir" (helper) is an intensive form of "nasir" (one who helps). It was said: "fa'il" here is in the sense of "maf'ul," i.e., "mansur" (one who is helped). All these sayings are possible for His words: ﴿a sultan, a helper﴾. (p-74) It is narrated that the Exalted One promised him this, fulfilled it for him during his life, and completed it after his death.

Qatadah said: "al-haqq" (the truth) is the Qur'an and "al-batil" (falsehood) is Satan. Ibn Jurayj said: "al-haqq" is jihad and "al-batil" is shirk. It was said: faith and disbelief. Muqatil said: the worship of Allah has come, and the worship of Satan has departed. This verse was revealed in Makkah. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to cite it on the day of the conquest of Makkah, when he struck the idols and they fell, by his striking them with a staff, as is mentioned in the biographies. "Zahuqan" (vanishing) is an intensive adjective describing its perishing and its not being established at any time.

The "min" in ﴿min al-Qur'an﴾ is for the beginning of the limit (ibtida' al-ghayah). It was said: it is for partitive (tab'id), said by al-Hawfi, but he denied this, since it entails that some of it has no healing in it; this denial was rejected, because its sending down is only in parts. It was said: it is for explaining the kind (bayan al-jins), said by al-Zamakhshari, Ibn 'Atiyyah and Abu al-Baqa'; and we have mentioned that "min" which is for explaining the kind does not precede the ambiguous term it clarifies, but is always placed after it. The majority read ﴿nunazzilu﴾ with a nun, and Mujahid with a ya' and lightened, which al-Marwazi narrated from Hafs. Zayd ibn 'Ali read ﴿shifa'an wa rahmatan﴾ with accusative on both; the accusative can be explained as a circumstantial accusative (hal), and the predicate of "huwa" is his saying "lil-mu'minin" (for the believers), and the governing element in it is the verb contained in the prepositional phrase, similar to the reading of one who read ﴿and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar: 67] with the accusative of "matwiyyat." And the poet's verse:

"The kinsmen of Ibn Kuz, wearing their armour, among them and the kinsmen of Rabi'ah ibn Hidhar."

Placing the circumstantial accusative before its governing element when it is an adverb or prepositional phrase is not permitted except according to al-Akhfash; whoever prohibits it makes it an accusative by an implied "a'ni" (I mean). Its healing is its being a remover of doubt and a uncoverer of the veil of the heart by grasping the miracles and the matters indicating Allah that establish His religion; thus it becomes for the ailments of hearts what healing is for the ailments of bodies. It was also said: it is healing by ruqyah and 'awdh (incantation), as in the hadith of the one who performed ruqyah with al-Fatihah for a scorpion's sting. They differed regarding al-nushrah, which is to write something of the names of Allah the Exalted or of the Qur'an, then wash it with water, then wipe the sick person with it or have him drink it; Ibn al-Musayyib permitted this, while Mujahid did not consider it. From 'A'ishah: she used to recite the two mu'awwidhatayn over a vessel, then instruct that it be poured over the sick person. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Mazini said: al-nushrah is a matter well known among the people of ta'widh (spells), named so because it "unties" (tanshuru) from its owner, i.e., it releases; al-Hasan and al-Nakha'i prohibited it. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Jabir that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when asked about al-nushrah, said: "It is from the work of Satan." This is to be understood as applying when it is outside what is in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger. Al-nushrah is of the kind of medicine in washing something that has merit.

Malik said: there is no harm in hanging books containing the names of Allah the Exalted on the necks of the sick, seeking blessing through them, provided the one who hangs them does not intend thereby to ward off the evil eye. This applies before any affliction of the evil eye has befallen; but after the affliction has come, it is permitted, hoping for relief and cure. Sickness is like the permitted ruqyah for which the Sunnah has come, from the evil eye and other things. Ibn al-Musayyib said: it is permitted to hang an 'awdhah (amulet) in a reed or a piece of paper from the Book of Allah, and one may place it when having intercourse and when relieving oneself. Al-Baqir permitted an 'awdhah hung on children. Ibn Sirin saw no harm in a person hanging something from the Qur'an.

And the loss of the wrongdoers, who are those who place a thing in other than its place, is through their turning away from it and not reflecting upon it, unlike the believer, for he increases in faith by looking into it and reflecting upon its meanings.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 17, verse 78–86 (part 1 of 3):

﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.﴾ ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud (voluntary night prayer) with it as an additional devotion for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.﴾ ﴿And say: "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself an authority to help me."﴾ ﴿And say: "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish."﴾ ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾ ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself, and when evil touches him, he is ever despairing.﴾ ﴿Say: "Each acts according to his manner, but your Lord knows best who is best guided in way."﴾ ﴿And they ask you about the soul. Say: "The soul is of the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little."﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you; then you would not find for yourself against Us any advocate,﴾ ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His favor upon you has ever been great.﴾ [al-Isra': 87] ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants."﴾ [al-Isra': 88] ﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every example, but most of the people refused except disbelief.﴾ [al-Isra': 89] ﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause to gush forth for us a spring from the earth,﴾ [al-Isra': 90] ﴿or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes and make rivers gush forth within it in abundance,﴾ [al-Isra': 91] ﴿or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments as you claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee,﴾ [al-Isra': 92] ﴿or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I but a human messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 93] ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 94] ﴿Say: "If there were in the earth angels walking calmly, We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger."﴾ [al-Isra': 95] ﴿Say: "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever Acquainted with and Seeing of His servants."﴾ [al-Isra': 96] ﴿And whomever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, and whomever He sends astray, you will not find for them protectors apart from Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind and mute and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; whenever its fire subsides, We increase for them its blaze.﴾ [al-Isra': 97] ﴿That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, "When we are bones and crumbled remains, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ [al-Isra': 98] ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is Able to create their likes? And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, but the wrongdoers refused except disbelief.﴾ [al-Isra': 99] ﴿Say: "If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold them for fear of expenditure. And man has ever been tight-fisted."﴾ [al-Isra': 100] ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched."﴾ [al-Isra': 101] ﴿He said, "You have certainly known that these have not sent down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence, and indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed."﴾ [al-Isra': 102] ﴿So he intended to expel them from the land, but We drowned him and whoever was with him, all together.﴾ [al-Isra': 103] ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, "Dwell in the land; and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed multitude."﴾ [al-Isra': 104] ﴿And with truth We sent it down, and with truth it descended, and We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.﴾ [al-Isra': 105] ﴿And a Qur'an which We have separated that you may recite it to the people over a duration, and We have sent it down in stages.﴾ [al-Isra': 106] ﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration,﴾ [al-Isra': 107] ﴿and say, "Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has ever been fulfilled."﴾ [al-Isra': 108] ﴿And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.﴾ [al-Isra': 109] ﴿Say: "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call, to Him belong the most beautiful names." And do not recite your prayer aloud or quietly, but seek between that a middle way.﴾ [al-Isra': 110] ﴿And say: "Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and has no protector out of weakness," and glorify Him with great glorification.﴾ [al-Isra': 111]

(The commentary on the words of Allah, "Establish prayer...") The connection of ﴿Establish prayer﴾ with what precedes it is that when He mentioned their plotting against the Messenger and what they intended by it, He commanded him to turn to his own affair of worshipping his Lord and not to occupy his heart with them. The discussion had already preceded concerning theology, the return (resurrection), and prophethood, so He followed that with the command to the most noble of acts of worship and obedience after faith, which is prayer. The discussion of establishing prayer has already occurred, and the address of the command was directed to the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace. The lam in ﴿li-dulūki﴾ — they said it means "after," i.e., after the decline (dulūk) of the sun, as they said this regarding the people of Mutammim ibn Nuwayra, lamenting his brother Malik:

"When we separated, it was as though I and Malik, after a long gathering, had not spent a single night together."

I.e., after a long gathering. And from this (usage) is his writing "on the third of such and such month" (lithalāth khalawna min shahr kadhā). Al-Wahidi said: the lam is for causation, because prayer becomes obligatory only with the decline of the sun, so it is obligatory upon the one praying to establish it because of the decline of the sun. Ibn Atiyya said: ﴿Establish prayer﴾ and the rest of the verse — this, by consensus of the exegetes, refers to the obligatory prayers. Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Burda, al-Hasan and the majority said: the decline of the sun is its passing the zenith, and the reference is to Dhuhr and 'Asr; and the darkness of the night refers to Maghrib and 'Isha'. ﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾ is intended to mean the Subh prayer, so the verse according to this encompasses all the prayers.

Ibn Mas'ud narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me at the decline of the sun when it passed the zenith, and he led me in the Dhuhr prayer." Jabir narrated that the Prophet ﷺ went out from his place after eating, and the sun had passed its zenith, and he said: "Go out, O Abu Bakr, for this is the time when the sun has declined." Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam said: the decline of the sun is its setting, and the reference by it is to Maghrib; (and the darkness of the night) is its gloom, so the reference is to 'Atama (the night prayer). ﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾ is the Subh prayer, and no reference according to this interpretation is made to Dhuhr and 'Asr. End. And from Ali it is reported that it is the setting. The lam and ilā are connected to aqim, so ilā is a limit for establishing (the prayer). Abu al-Baqa' permitted that it be a circumstantial accusative (hal) of the prayer, saying: meaning "extended." By "the recitation of dawn" he means the Subh prayer, and it was singled out with the word "Qur'an," which is recitation, because its recitation is great, since its recitation is long and loudly voiced. ﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾ is in the accusative as a conjunction to (al-salāh, "the prayer").

Al-Akhfash said: it is in the accusative by an implied verb, its estimate being "and devote yourself to the recitation of dawn" or "upon you is the recitation of dawn." End. The Subh prayer was named after some of what occurs in it. Al-Zamakhshari said: the Fajr prayer was named "Qur'an," which is recitation, because it is a pillar, just as it was named ruku' (bowing), sujud (prostration) and qunut (devout standing), and it is a proof against Ibn Abi Ulayya and al-Asamm in their claim that recitation is not a pillar. End. It was said: if we interpret dulūk as the decline of the sun, the time becomes shared between Dhuhr and 'Asr, when the establishment is limited by the darkness of the night, and the darkness (ghasaq) becomes a time shared between Maghrib and 'Isha'; and the mentioned would be three times: the beginning of the time of decline, the beginning of the time of Maghrib, and the beginning of the time of Fajr. End. What the apparent wording indicates is that it is a command to establish prayer either from the beginning of the decline until the darkness, and with the recitation of dawn; or from the setting until the darkness and with the recitation of dawn. Thus the thing commanded is prayer at two times, and the times of the five prayers are not derived from this wording in any way.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said, regarding His words ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn﴾, that it is evidence that the prayer is not complete except with recitation, because the command is for obligation, and recitation at that time is obligatory only within prayer. Whoever says that the meaning of ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn﴾ is the dawn prayer has erred, because he has turned the speech from its literal meaning to the figurative without evidence. Also, in the sequence of the recitation comes ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it as a supererogatory prayer for you﴾, and it is impossible to perform tahajjud with the dawn prayer at night. The pronoun in (bihi, "with it") refers to ﴿the Qur'an of dawn﴾ mentioned before it, so it is established that the intended meaning is the very Qur'an, not the place of tahajjud with the recited Qur'an in the dawn prayer, nor the impossibility of tahajjud at night with the dawn prayer. And even if it were possible for the intended meaning to be what they mentioned, its evidence would still stand for the obligation of recitation in prayer, because recitation was never used as an expression for prayer except that it is one of its pillars. End. There is some abridgement in it.

The apparent meaning is that it is recommended (nadb) to perform the dawn prayer at the beginning of its time, because He commanded the performance of ﴿the Qur'an of dawn﴾, so it would require obligation at the first emergence of dawn. But consensus (ijma') prevented that, so the recommendation remained, due to the existence of the requirement, and when its obligation is removed, its recommendation remains. He repeated ﴿the Qur'an of dawn﴾ in His words ﴿Indeed, the Qur'an of dawn﴾ and did not use a pronoun, which indicates the honouring and highlighting of the Qur'an of dawn. The meaning of ﴿mashhudan﴾ ("witnessed") is that it is witnessed by the angels, the guardians of the night and the guardians of the day, as came in the hadith: "They succeed one another, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer." This is the view of the majority. It has been said: it is witnessed by many of the worshippers customarily. It has also been said: it is required that a large congregation witness it. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn﴾ is an exhortation to lengthen the recitation in the dawn prayer, since it is a prayer in which people are gathered so that they hear the Qur'an and the reward increases; for this reason the dawn prayer was the longest of the prayers in recitation. End. By his words "an exhortation" he means that the implied sense is: "and upon you [is] the Qur'an of dawn," or "and keep to it."

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn 'Askar said: ﴿mashhudan﴾ means that Allah and His angels witness it, and he mentioned the hadith of Abu al-Darda', that He descends in the last part of the night. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi has a discussion regarding His words ﴿mashhudan﴾ according to his habit in interpreting the Book of Allah in ways the Arabs would not understand. What should be followed, indeed what must not be deviated from, is what the Messenger (ﷺ) explained it with, when he said regarding it: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it." At-Tirmidhi said of it: a hadith, hasan sahih.

When Allah commanded him to establish the prayer at the stated time, and His command did not indicate that it was specific to him to the exclusion of his community, He mentioned what He singled him out for and made obligatory upon him from qiyam al-layl, which for his community is voluntary. So He said: ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it﴾, i.e., with the Qur'an in prayer, ﴿as a supererogatory prayer (nafilah) for you﴾, specifically for you. Here tahajjud is of the form tafa''ala in the sense of removal and abandonment, like their saying: ta'atthama and tahannatha meaning "he abandoned sin" and "he abandoned the taḥannuth," and from it: "I tahannathtu in the cave of Hira'," i.e., I abandoned the taḥannuth; and it is explained by its implication, which is worship (al-ta'abbud). ("From") here is for partitive meaning (lil-tab'id).

Al-Hawfi said: "from" is connected to a verb indicated by the meaning of the speech, its estimate being: "and stay awake from the night with the Qur'an." He said: It is possible that the estimate be: "and rise after a sleep from the night." Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "from" is partitive; the estimate is "a time of the night," i.e., "and rise a time of the night." Al-Zamakhshari said: "and from the night" means "and upon you [is] part of the night, ﴿so perform tahajjud with it﴾," and tahajjud is abandoning sleep for prayer. End.
